<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The number of shares
outstanding of the registrant&#146;s Common Stock as of December&nbsp;18, 2009 was
10,262,430.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PART&nbsp;I</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 1.&#160; BUSINESS</font></b></h3>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Development
and Description of Business</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">XETA Technologies,&nbsp;Inc.
(&#147;XETA&#148;, the &#147;Company&#148;, &#147;we&#148;, &#147;us&#148;, or &#147;our&#148;), an Oklahoma corporation formed
in 1981, is a leading integrator of advanced communications technologies with
nationwide sales and service.&nbsp; XETA provides sales, design, project
management, implementation, and maintenance services in support of the products
it represents.&#160; The Company sells
products produced by several manufacturers including Avaya,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Avaya&#148;),
Nortel Networks Corporation (&#147;Nortel&#148;), Mitel Corporation (&#147;Mitel&#148;), and
Samsung Business Communications Systems (&#147;Samsung&#148;).&#160; In addition, the Company manufactures and
markets a line of proprietary call accounting systems to the hospitality
industry.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We market our products
and services to a variety of companies such as enterprise-class multi-location,
mid market and large companies located throughout the United States.&nbsp; We
also market our solutions and services to several vertical markets such as
hospitality, education, Federal government, and healthcare.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We deliver services
through our nationwide network of Company-employed design engineers, service
technicians and qualified third party service providers.&#160; Our service delivery is coordinated in our
contact center, which operates 24-hours per day, 7-days-per-week and is located
at our headquarters in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma. Our contact center and national
technical footprint are well-suited to address the communication needs of
large, multi-location, national, or super-regional customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Large enterprises often
have a combination of manufacturer platforms in their communications equipment
portfolios.&nbsp; As such our ability to sell and service three of the leading
communication platforms is an important competitive advantage.&nbsp; Because of
our extensive array of products and services, we enjoy multiple sales
opportunities with these customers.&nbsp; These include new equipment
installations, implementation of advanced applications, and various service
relationships.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">An important element of
our sales strategy is to continually search for opportunities to expand
business relationships with current customers. Our sales teams continually
monitor and assess our customer&#146;s communications needs, proposing appropriate
technologies to address those needs, establishing or expanding the service
relationship, and proposing equipment and service solutions to other divisions
or subsidiaries.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under our wholesale
services offering, we collaborate with manufacturers, network service providers
and systems integrators to provide services to their end-user customers.&nbsp;
In many instances, we provide field resources to carry out on-site service
activities.&nbsp; Under a full outsourcing arrangement we may provide a broader
range of services.&#160; These services
include call center support, remote technical support, on-site labor and spare
parts.&nbsp; Our wholesale services business initiative has succeeded because
we provide excellent service to end-user customers, and are willing to create
and execute flexible service programs and billing arrangements.&nbsp; The
continued success of our wholesale services initiative is a vital component of
our long-term goal of shifting our revenue mix toward more services revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April, 2009, we signed
a three year services collaboration and dealer agreement with Samsung.&#160; Under the agreement, our professional
services team supports Samsung&#146;s North American channel partners and customers.
The Samsung delivery team utilizes a &#147;Center of Excellence&#148; model that
encourages knowledge sharing and ongoing review of best practices.&#160; The model ensures the highest level of
service to dealers and end-users alike.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We strive to align our
Company&#146;s sales, marketing, and services programs with those of our
manufacturing partners.&nbsp; As the composition of the market evolves in
response to Avaya&#146;s acquisition of Nortel, our cogent and well crafted sales
plan is of even greater importance.&#160; We
have developed sales and service programs to assist customers in supporting
their existing investments or migrating their portfolios to alternative
technologies.&#160; Our sales teams will
continue to search for market opportunities resulting from the consolidation of
Avaya and Nortel.&#160; Uncertainties in the
market may also result in acceleration in our acquisitions particularly in the
Nortel partner community.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3<a name="PB_3_105818_5335"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commercial Systems Sales</font></i></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We sell communications
solutions to the commercial market, school districts, the Federal government,
and to the healthcare market.&nbsp; These solutions are designed to maximize
the effectiveness of our customers&#146; communications systems through the use of
advanced technologies.&nbsp;&#160; By
deploying advanced communications technologies and consolidating voice and data
traffic on a common infrastructure our customers can reduce their total
communications costs.&#160; In addition,
through the use of integrated applications they can also improve employee
productivity.&nbsp; With the adoption of IP telephony by most enterprise level
customers, new, advanced applications such as Unified Communications systems
and collaboration software are widely available.&nbsp; These advanced applications
combine voice, voice mail, presence, instant messaging, and video applications
and seamlessly integrates them on the desktop with other data applications such
as MS Outlook&#153;.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We sell these systems
under dealer agreements with Avaya, Nortel and Mitel.&nbsp; These manufacturers
have significant installed bases in the communications equipment market and are
migrating their customers from traditional telephony systems to server based
platforms.&nbsp; To support our sales efforts we receive incentive payments
from the manufacturers to offset certain product costs, training expenses, and
specific sales and marketing expenses.&nbsp; We purchase Avaya and Nortel
products through major distributors and receive additional price incentives
from these distributors.&nbsp; These incentive payments are material to our
business.&nbsp; We purchase Mitel systems directly from Mitel to receive
additional discounts.&nbsp; We sell data networking products to the commercial
market under non-exclusive dealer agreements with Avaya, Nortel, Samsung,
Juniper Systems, Cisco Systems Inc., and Hewlett-Packard Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Hospitality Products</font></i></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Communications
Systems</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; We
sell communications systems to the hospitality industry through nationwide,
non-exclusive dealer agreements with Avaya, Nortel, and Mitel.&nbsp; In
addition to most of the features available on commercial systems, the systems
sold to hospitality customers include hospitality-specific software, which
integrates with nearly all aspects of the property&#146;s operations.&nbsp; We also
offer a variety of related products such as voice mail systems, analog
telephones, uninterruptible power supplies, announcement systems, and others,
most of which also have hospitality-specific features.&nbsp; The majority of
these additional products are sold in conjunction with the sale of new
communications systems and, with the exception of voicemail systems, are
purchased from regional and national suppliers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Call Accounting
Products</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;
We sell a line of proprietary call accounting products under the Virtual XL</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and Virtual
XL.2&#153; product names.&nbsp; Introduced in 1998, the &#147;VXL&#148; series is a PC-based
system designed to operate on a property&#146;s local or wide area network.&nbsp; If
that network is connected to the Internet, the VXL can also be accessed via an
Internet connection.&nbsp; The original VXL was upgraded to a rack-mounted,
server-style system in 2004 and is marketed under the name Virtual XL.2&#153;&nbsp;(&#147;VXL&#148;).&#160; The VXL systems are our latest in a series of
call accounting products we have successfully marketed since the Company&#146;s
inception.&nbsp; Many of those earlier products remain in operation at customer
locations and are under maintenance contracts with us or generate
time-and-materials (&#147;T&amp;M&#148;) revenues.&nbsp; These revenues and the related
gross profits are material to our business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sales of communications
systems and products to the hospitality industry represented 13%, 10%, and 11%
of total revenues in fiscal 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&nbsp; Marriott
International, Host Marriott, and other Marriott-affiliated companies (&#147;Marriott&#148;)
represent a single customer relationship for our Company and a major
contributor to our hospitality revenues.&nbsp; Revenues earned from sales of
hospitality systems sold to Marriott represented 20%, 21%, and 32% of our sales
of hospitality systems in fiscal 2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Services</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Services revenue is our
largest revenue stream.&nbsp; Because a majority of these revenues are
recurring and produce generally higher margins, this portion of our business is
of vital importance to our operating results.&nbsp; Our services offerings
includes nation-wide customer service, project management, professional
services, installation, consulting, and structured cabling
implementation.&nbsp; The geographic reach and technical breadth of our
services organization are key differentiators between us and our competitors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our services organization
includes our National Service Center (&#147;NSC&#148;) located at our headquarters in
Broken Arrow, Oklahoma.&nbsp; The NSC supports our commercial and hospitality
customers who have purchased maintenance contracts on their systems, as well as
other customers who engage us on hourly time-and-material or per occurrence
basis.&nbsp; We employ a network of highly trained technicians who are
strategically located in major metropolitan areas and can be dispatched to customer
locations or to install new systems.&nbsp; We also employ design and
implementation engineers, referred to as our Professional Services Organization
(&#147;PSO&#148;), to design voice, data, and converged solutions to meet specific
customer requirements.&nbsp; Much of the work done by the PSO is pre-sales
design and is often not recovered in revenues.&#160;
While this activity represents a significant investment, we believe that
by hiring the most qualified personnel possible to provide these services we
create a competitive advantage.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">4<a name="PB_4_105837_5796"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For Avaya, Nortel, and
Mitel communications systems sold to hospitality customers, we sell XETA
maintenance contracts.&nbsp; For our proprietary products, we offer
post-warranty service contracts under one-year and multi-year service
contracts.&nbsp; The revenues earned from the sale of our maintenance contracts
are an important part of our business model as they provide a predictable
stream of profitable recurring revenue.&nbsp; We earn a significant portion of
our repair and maintenance services revenues from hospitality customers who
maintain service contracts on their systems.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To our non-hospitality
end-users of Nortel equipment, we sell XETA maintenance contracts.&nbsp;
Additionally, we aggressively market our services capabilities to existing and
potential wholesale customers.&nbsp; Our largest wholesale customer is
Nortel.&nbsp; Nortel has maintenance contracts with many &#147;Fortune 1000&#148;
customers and outsources much of the on-site service work to authorized service
providers, such as XETA.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For Avaya products sold
to non-hospitality customers, we sell Avaya&#146;s post-warranty maintenance
contracts, for which we earn a commission.&nbsp; These commissions are recorded
as &#147;Other Revenues&#148; in our financial statements and are material to our gross
profits and net income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For our distributed
products, we pass on the manufacturer&#146;s limited warranty, which is generally
one year in length.&nbsp; Labor costs associated with fulfilling the warranty
requirements are generally borne by us.&nbsp; For our proprietary call
accounting products sold to the hospitality industry, we provide a limited
one-year parts and labor warranty.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Marketing</font></i></b></h1>

<h1 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We market our products
and services primarily through our direct sales force to a wide variety of
customers including large national companies, mid-size companies, hospitality
industry, education market, Federal government, and the healthcare
industry.&nbsp; Because the technology we sell is typically an application
running on an existing data network, the focus of our marketing efforts has had
to adjust toward data networking decision makers, many of whom are at the
executive level of their organization.&nbsp; These executives may have
long-standing relationships with their data products and services dealers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to marketing
directly to end-users, we also have a significant sales and marketing effort
dedicated to our wholesale services.&nbsp; This area of our business has
experienced significant growth in recent years and is a key contributor to our
increase in services revenues.&nbsp; Under these offerings we partner with
manufacturers, network services companies, and systems integrators to provide a
variety of technical services to our partners&#146; end-user customers.&nbsp; We
make considerable investments in sales and technical resources to create
relationships with current and potential wholesale partners.&nbsp; Once those
relationships are established, we jointly market our capabilities with our
partners to end-users who have requested bids for new services or are renewing
existing contracts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Another important aspect
of our marketing effort centers on our relationships with our
manufacturers.&nbsp; As a national dealer, we have certain technical and
geographical capabilities that help differentiate us in the marketplace and we
aggressively market these capabilities to Avaya, Nortel, and Mitel.&nbsp; The
manufacturers utilize us in a variety of ways, from fulfilling certain customer
orders to handling entire customer relationships.&nbsp; We have carefully
positioned ourselves as a leading dealer by achieving the highest level of
certification with each manufacturer, building our in-house engineering
capabilities, providing nationwide implementation services, and through access
to our 24-hour, 7 days-per-week service center.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our marketing efforts to the hospitality industry rely heavily on our
experience and reputation in that industry.&nbsp; Over the course of serving
this market for more than 28 years, we have built strong long-term
relationships with a wide range of key decision makers responsible for the purchase
of hotel communications technology.&nbsp; We have relationships with nearly all
hotel chains and major hospitality property management companies.&nbsp; We
target our hospitality marketing efforts at strengthening and deepening these
relationships.&nbsp; The addition of the Mitel product line has also allowed us
to expand our already leading market position by providing us an opportunity to
talk with hospitality industry buying channels that have previously
standardized on the Mitel product line and were not previously potential
customers for us.&nbsp; It has also given us the opportunity to approach
existing customers about additional hotel segments that require a lower price
point communications server.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5<a name="PB_5_105854_2897"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Competition</font></i></b></h1>

<h1 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commercial</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; The market for Commercial
communications systems, applications and services is rapidly evolving due to
the convergence of voice and data networks and the speed at which new
applications are being introduced.&nbsp; Our market has always been highly competitive,
as both Avaya and Nortel have extensive dealer organizations, including the
Regional Bell Operating Companies, nationwide dealers similar to us, and
smaller regional dealers.&nbsp; In addition to Avaya and Nortel dealers, we
also face competition from dealers of other communications&#146; technology
manufacturers such as Cisco Systems,&nbsp;Inc., ShorTel,&nbsp;Inc., and NEC
Corporation.&nbsp; With the addition of data products dealers, particularly
Cisco dealers, competition has increased.&nbsp; Many of our new competitors
have long-standing relationships with the Information Technology (&#147;IT&#148;)
decision makers of our customers, increasing the ferocity of the competition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Hospitality</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; We face similar competitive
pressures to those discussed above in our hospitality business.&nbsp; However,
since the hospitality market is a small niche market, we believe our most
effective advantages are the performance and reliability of our proprietary
call accounting systems and our high level of service commitment to this niche
market.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We assemble the Virtual
XL</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and Virtual XL.2&#153; systems, our proprietary
call accounting systems, which are sold exclusively to the hospitality
industry.&nbsp; We assemble these systems from an inventory of components,
parts and sub-assemblies obtained from various suppliers.&nbsp; These components
are purchased from a variety of regional and national distributors at prices
that fluctuate based on demand and volumes purchased.&nbsp; Some components,
although widely distributed, are manufactured by a single, usually foreign,
source and are therefore subject to shortages and price fluctuations if
manufacturing is interrupted.&nbsp; We maintain adequate inventories of
components to mitigate short-term shortages and believe the ultimate risk of
long-term shortages is minimal.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of the other products
we sell are purchased as finished goods from the manufacturers&#146; distributors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Employees</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We employed 372 and 361
employees at December&nbsp;1, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h4 align="left" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Copyrights,
Patents and Trademarks</font></i></b></h4>

<h4 align="left" style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h4>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We own registered United
States trademarks on the following names for use in the marketing of our
hospitality services and systems: &#147;XETA,&#148; &#147;XPERT,&#148; &#147;XL,&#148; and &#147;Virtual XL&#148;.&nbsp;
All of these trademarks are on the principal register of the United States
Patent and Trademark Office.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6<a name="PB_6_105908_3020"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 1A.&#160; RISK FACTORS</font></b></h3>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business and
prospects are subject to risks and uncertainties. The following items are
representative of the risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could affect
our business, future performance and the outcome of our forward-looking
statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Nortel&#146;s Chapter 11 Bankruptcy
filing and subsequent sale of its enterprise solution business to Avaya may
negatively impact our revenues and/or financial condition.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Nortel filed a voluntary
petition for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on January&nbsp;14, 2009.&#160; To date Nortel has not filed its plan of
reorganization.&#160; In the meantime the
administrators of the bankruptcy have adopted a business disposal strategy,
pursuant to which they have sold the Nortel enterprise solution business (&#147;NES&#148;)
to Avaya.&#160; All of the foregoing
developments pose a variety of risks to our business, as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Throughout fiscal 2009 uncertainty
surrounding Nortel&#146;s bankruptcy significantly dampened demand for equipment in
this product line.&nbsp; Until Nortel files it plan of reorganization, this
uncertainty is likely to continue.&#160;
Nortel has until February&nbsp;1, 2010 to file its plan of
reorganization unless such date is further extended by the court.&#160; Although Avaya&#146;s acquisition of Nortel&#146;s
enterprise division may help to reduce the uncertainly in the market over the
course of fiscal 2010, in the near term we anticipate continued weakness in
demand for Nortel equipment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are owed approximately $700,000 in pre-petition
accounts receivable less approximately $116,000 in approved offsets for amounts
we owed to Nortel at the time of the filing.&#160;
If our pre-petition claims are not collectible either in whole or in
large part, we could experience material, negative operating results in the
near term.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Nortel has filed a statement of financial affairs
under which it shows payments to the Company against multiple invoices of
approximately $1.6 million which were made during the 90-day statutory &#147;preference
period&#148; under bankruptcy law.&#160; As such,
these payments are considered &#147;preference payments&#148; and are subject to a &#147;preference
claim&#148; which can be asserted by Nortel.&#160;&#160;
Bankruptcy law allows the debtor to recover these payments unless the
creditor successfully establishes that the payments were made in the ordinary
course of business between the debtor and creditor.&#160; If Nortel elects to assert a preference claim
against the Company for this amount or any portion thereof and the Company is
unable to successfully defend the claim, the Company would have to return any
such amounts to Nortel.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Avaya&#146;s purchase of NES&#151;which is one of our major
suppliers, is an important customer, and whose product line represents a
significant portion of our business&#151;may result in a significant disruption
and/or material decline in our revenues and gross profits.&#160; Avaya and NES are large, complex companies
with global operations.&#160; They have had
very different marketing strategies and both have long, deep cultural
traditions.&#160; The integration of these two
companies will be challenging and disruptive to the market.&#160; There can be no assurance given that the
combination of Avaya and NES will not have near-term and/or long-term material,
negative impact on our operating results, financial position, market position,
and overall reputation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our
business is affected by capital spending.&#160;
Economic conditions and the continued difficulty for our customers to
access affordable credit may inhibit capital spending over the next twelve
months and beyond.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The U.S. economy is still
struggling to emerge from a severe recessionary contraction.&#160; Despite efforts by the Federal Government to
stabilize the banking and financial systems, credit availability remains
limited for nearly all enterprises.&#160;
Hence the outlook for corporate capital investment is uncertain.&nbsp;
These factors contribute to a high degree of uncertainty concerning capital
spending.&#160; Because our business relies on
capital spending for technology and equipment, we may continue to experience
declining demand for our products.&#160; This
could have a material, negative impact on our operating results and financial
condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We may
experience higher than normal bad debt losses as a result of economic
conditions and may experience lower revenues as a result of limiting our
extension of credit to customers.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The recent economic
downturn and tight credit markets have resulted in some of our customers
experiencing difficulty in paying their obligations to us, particularly
obligations related to the purchase of new systems.&#160; While we monitor credit reports and payment
histories carefully, we cannot eliminate all of the risks associated with the
extension of credit.&#160; As a result, we may
experience higher rates of bad debt in the near future and we may also
experience lower revenues as a result of tightening our credit standards.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">7<a name="PB_7_105937_7748"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our
revenue for a particular period is difficult to predict, and a shortfall in
revenue can harm our operating results.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our systems sales,
implementation, cabling, and other revenues for a particular quarter are
difficult to predict.&nbsp; Our total revenues may decline or grow at a slower
rate than in past periods.&nbsp; We have experienced periods during which
shipments have exceeded net bookings, or manufacturing issues have delayed
shipments, resulting in erratic revenues.&nbsp; The timing of orders, primarily
in our systems sales, can also impact our quarter to quarter business and
operating results.&#160; As a result, our
operating results could vary materially from quarter to quarter based on the
receipt of orders, and the ultimate recognition of revenue.&nbsp; We set our
operating expenses based primarily on forecasted revenues.&nbsp; An unexpected
shortfall in revenues could lead to lower than expected operating results if we
are unable to quickly reduce these fixed expenses in response to short-term
business changes.&nbsp; Any of these factors could have a material adverse
impact on our operations and financial results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The lack
of available credit beyond our current credit facility may impair our ability
to fully execute our acquisition growth strategies.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our growth strategy
includes the acquisition of businesses that either increase our market share in
traditional voice or converged communications systems or expand our
competencies and presence in advanced technologies such as Unified
Communications and collaboration applications.&#160;
The economic downturn, the cost of entry into these new communications
applications businesses, and the acquisition of NES by Avaya has increased the
number of potential acquisition opportunities for us.&#160; However, because of the continued uncertainty
in the credit markets and the lack of credit available through traditional
lending institutions, it may be difficult for us to finance the acquisition
opportunities available with senior debt.&nbsp; Despite our strong cash flows
and low debt, our ability to secure senior debt financing is subject to the
same limitations and costs affecting the market as a whole.&#160; There is no assurance that alternative
sources of capital will be sufficient to pursue all the acquisition
opportunities considered in the best interest of the Company.&nbsp; As a result
we may be unable to pursue certain reasonably priced, synergistic opportunities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The
value of our product and services offerings to the hospitality market is
declining and our repair and maintenance revenues associated with this line of
business are under significant pressure.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Increasing use of cell
phones by guests has caused a rapid decline in hotels&#146; revenues and gross
profits earned from long distance and other telephone-related fees. &nbsp;This
development has severely reduced the importance of PBX and call accounting
systems in hotels.&nbsp; Additionally, many of the new voice applications have
limited value in the hospitality market.&nbsp; As a result, there is not a
compelling financial reason or guest-driven need to replace existing
equipment.&nbsp; The primary uses of guest room phones are to access hotel
amenities such as the front desk or room service or to call other guests.&nbsp;
Additionally, guest room phones are necessary to satisfy laws mandating access
to 911 services in all guest rooms.&nbsp; Manufacturers who enjoy a significant
share of the installed base of systems in the hospitality market are in
competition with startup firms to develop low cost, shared, network dial tone
that will meet the needs of hotel properties at prices that will produce a
sufficient return on their investment.&nbsp; While we are carefully monitoring
these developments, there is no assurance that hotels spending on PBX and call
accounting systems and associated maintenance services will not drop
dramatically resulting in a material, negative impact on our operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Success
in our overall strategy, a key component of which is to focus on the marketing
of advanced communications products and applications and related services, may
be difficult or even prevented by a variety of factors.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expansion of our net
profit margins and increasing our shareholders&#146; return on investment over the
long term is highly dependent upon our ability to become a leader in the sale,
implementation, and ongoing maintenance of advanced communications.&nbsp;
Because of their sophistication and complex integration with both network and desktop
software applications, including Microsoft Office products such as Outlook,
these products are expected to earn higher margins than our current
products.&nbsp; To succeed in these dynamic markets, we must continue to:&nbsp;
train our sales employees on the capabilities and technical specifications of
these new technologies; train our services technicians to support these
products and applications; develop relationships with new types of qualified
service providers to supplement our internal capabilities; and develop new
relationships with different disciplines, and at higher management levels,
within our customers&#146; organizations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, because
many of these technologies are in the early stages of market acceptance, we
cannot predict whether: (i)&nbsp;the demand for advanced communications
products, applications, and services, including IP telephony systems and UC,
will grow as fast as anticipated; (ii)&nbsp;other new technologies may cause
the market to evolve in a manner different than we expect; or (iii)&nbsp;technologies
developed by manufacturers that we do not represent may become more accepted as
the industry standard.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8<a name="PB_8_105949_141"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Finally, we cannot
predict the impact of economic conditions on the adoption of these technologies.&nbsp;
We believe that most customers will likely limit their capital investments to
those with anticipated paybacks of one year or less until it is clearer that an
economic recovery is underway and competitive pressures begin to drive
technology decision-making again.&nbsp; While UC and other
collaboration-oriented voice applications are predicted to enhance user
productivity and improve the security of certain intra-company communications,
the return rate on these investments is yet unproven, therefore customers may
choose to delay investment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We may
experience severe declines in our services revenues from the loss of a major
wholesale services customer.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our wholesale services
revenues are generated from a few large customers who contract with us to
provide a variety of services for specific end-user customers.&nbsp; Typically,
the end-user customer is a large corporation as well.&nbsp; Our experience to
date in these arrangements indicates that we may experience severe reductions
in service revenues in the event that either the end-user or our customer
selects a different service provider or changes their operating strategy
regarding the delivery of these services.&nbsp; The loss of one of our
wholesale managed service customers could have a sudden, material, adverse effect
on our operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Avaya
has announced a significant change in their pricing structure and incentive
programs, which may affect our operating results.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Avaya has recently
announced significant changes in its pricing structure and incentive programs.&#160; According to Avaya these changes, which are
being made to simplify its pricing structure and eliminate the need to request
special discounts and administer complex incentive programs, should be neutral
to profit margins.&#160; Our initial review of
these changes contradicts Avaya&#146;s statements regarding the neutrality of these
changes on our profit margins.&#160; As a
large business partner of Avaya we receive substantial discounts off of list
price and the payments we receive under Avaya&#146;s various incentive programs are
material to our operating results.&#160; We
are continuing to evaluate these changes which are scheduled to take effect on February&nbsp;1,
2010.&#160; Avaya may make additional
adjustments to the announced changes before that date and/or may delay the
implementation of some or all of the changes as it continues to receive
feedback from its business partners.&#160; At
this time, no assurance can be given that the pricing and incentive program
changes eventually implemented by Avaya will not have a material, adverse impact
on our operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Avaya&#146;s strategies regarding the
provision of equipment and services to their customers are changing and could
have a material impact on our operating results.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Avaya is repositioning
itself as a hardware and software manufacturer providing a wide range of voice
communications hardware and applications to its customers.&#160; As part of this strategy, Avaya is segmenting
its hardware maintenance and software support.&#160;
The new software support offerings include technical support for specific
voice applications and upgrade services to ensure customers can access all
software patches and upgrades.&#160;
Currently, we earn revenues from some of our customers, particularly
hospitality customers, to provide the products and services now being included
by Avaya in its new software support offerings.&#160;
These changes could have a material, negative impact on our operating
results if our revenues or margins are reduced in response to these mandated
changes by Avaya.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We face
intense competition fueled by rapid changes in the technologies and markets in
which we operate.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The market for our
products and services is highly competitive and subject to rapidly changing
technologies.&nbsp; As the industry evolves and new technologies and products
are introduced, new participants enter the market and existing competitors
search for ways to strengthen their positions and expand their offerings.&nbsp;
There is a developing trend toward consolidation, which could result in the
creation of stronger competitors better able to compete as a sole-source vendor
for customers.&nbsp; While we believe that through our transformation and
expansion during the last few years, we are well positioned to compete
effectively in the marketplace; our failure to maintain or enhance this position
could adversely affect our business and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The
success of our business depends on our ability to recruit and retain highly
skilled personnel.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability to attract,
train, motivate and retain highly skilled and qualified technical and sales
personnel is critical to our success.&nbsp; Competition for such employees in
the rapidly changing communications industry is fierce.&nbsp; As we have
transformed our company into an integrator of advanced communications solutions
we have invested heavily in the hiring and training of personnel to sell and
service our portfolio of products and services.&nbsp; If we are unable to
retain our skilled employees or to hire additional qualified personnel when
needed, it could adversely impact our ability to implement our strategies.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9<a name="PB_9_110003_7608"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The
technology we sell is highly complex and changes rapidly, increasing our
reliance upon the manufacturers for technical assistance and increasing the
risk that our inventories on hand will become obsolete.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The communications
equipment we sell is highly complex and requires significant technical
resources to design, install, and maintain.&nbsp; This complexity may require
us to rely heavily upon the manufacturers&#146; technical staff to support the
installation and maintenance of communications systems.&nbsp; This reliance may
result in lower services revenue or lower profit margins earned on our services
revenue.&nbsp; In addition to their complexity, the systems are evolving
rapidly as product enhancements are introduced by the manufacturers.&nbsp;
These rapid changes present risks that our inventory on hand will become
obsolete, resulting in the need to reduce sales margins to sell the equipment
or in direct write-offs in the value of the equipment.&nbsp; Any of these
results would be detrimental to our profitability.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The loss
of our highest level dealer certifications with any of our manufacturers could
negatively impact our ability to differentiate our products and services in the
market and could negatively impact our operating results.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We hold the highest level
of dealer certifications with Avaya, Nortel, and Mitel.&nbsp; These
certifications are based on technical and sales capabilities and purchasing
volumes and are reviewed annually.&nbsp; We emphasize the fact that we are one
of the few providers in our market to have the highest certification level with
each manufacturer and we believe that this is a significant differentiator with
some customers who have two or more of the manufacturers&#146; products in their
installed base.&nbsp; Additionally, as a result of these certifications we
receive enhanced manufacturer incentive payments which are material to our
operating results.&nbsp; While we expect to maintain the technical
capabilities, sales skill sets, and purchasing volumes to secure our
certifications, a downgrade could have a material impact on our reputation in
the market and negatively impact our operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">The
introduction of new products could result in reduced revenues, reduced gross
margins, reduced customer satisfaction, and longer collection periods.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We sell a variety of
highly complex products that incorporate leading-edge hardware and software
technology.&nbsp; Early versions of these products, which we are selling
currently, can contain software defects or &#147;bugs&#148; that can cause the products
to not function as intended.&nbsp; We will be dependent upon our suppliers of
these technologies to fix these problem.&#160;&#160;
The inability of the manufacturer to quickly correct these problems could
result in damage to our reputation, reduced revenues, reduced customer
satisfaction, delays in payments from customers for products purchased, and
potential liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Compliance
with new corporate governance and accounting regulations may require a material
increase in our operating expenses beginning in fiscal 2010.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are required to comply
with a host of government-mandated corporate governance and accounting
regulations, the most significant of which is section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley
Act of 2002.&nbsp; Under the current guidelines issued by the Securities and
Exchange Commission, our auditors must attest on our report on internal
controls over financial reporting beginning in the year ended October&nbsp;31,
2010.&nbsp;&nbsp; In addition, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;)
has issued new accounting standards related to fair value and business
combination accounting.&nbsp; These rules&nbsp;require significantly different
accounting treatment for some items that are common in business combinations
and as such, our financial results could be materially different for future
acquisitions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A
significant portion of our expected growth in services revenues is dependent
upon our relationship with a few wholesale customers.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Much of the growth in our
services revenue is coming from a few wholesale service customers using us as a
subcontractor to service many of their high profile end-user customers.&nbsp;
We believe our relationship with these companies is strong and our performance
ratings have been excellent.&nbsp; However, our experience is that end-users&#146;
decisions to maintain their service agreements with our wholesale service
customers depends on factors which are beyond our control.&nbsp; Therefore we
can provide no assurance that we will not experience sudden declines in our
maintenance and repair services revenues due to the loss of large contracts by
our wholesale customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Hitachi&#146;s
decision to cease manufacturing communications systems for the hospitality
market has caused some uncertainty with respect to our future relationship with
our Hitachi installed base of hospitality customers.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Hitachi, once one of the
leading suppliers of traditional PBX systems to the hospitality market, ceased
selling systems to this market in March&nbsp;2005.&nbsp; We have many long-time
hospitality customers with significant portfolios of Hitachi systems in their
properties.&nbsp; In addition, we have several hundred Hitachi systems under
service contracts generating recurring contract revenues and gross
profits.&nbsp; Over the next four to six years, most of these customers will
have to transition their communications systems to new platforms.&#160; The transition presents a risk to us that
another vendor may be selected to install and service their communications
systems.&nbsp; In response we have added the Mitel product line to mitigate the
impact to our operating results due to Hitachi&#146;s exit from the hospitality
market.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10<a name="PB_10_110020_8146"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
