<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While Hitachi&#146;s exit
created some uncertainty in our relationship with existing customers, we
believe our relationship with our Hitachi customers is strong.&nbsp;
Consequently, we believe that in most instances we will be in a favorable
position to supply a new system to our customers when they decide to replace
their Hitachi system.&nbsp; Additionally, during the third quarter of fiscal
2006 we acquired the remaining assets and liabilities of Hitachi&#146;s U.S.
hospitality market.&nbsp; Included in the acquired assets was a substantial
inventory of new and refurbished parts and equipment enabling us to serve our
Hitachi customers.&nbsp; Despite these mitigating factors, no assurance can be
given that Hitachi&#146;s exit from this market will not negatively impact our
financial results in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We are
connecting our products to our customer&#146;s computer networks and integrating
these products to other customer-owned software applications such as the
Microsoft Office Suite.&nbsp; In most cases, we are integrating our products to
mission-critical networks and systems such as contact centers owned by the
customer.&nbsp; Problems with the implementation of these products could cause
operational disruption, loss of revenues and gross profits for our customers.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unlike traditional
stand-alone voice systems, new IP-based products and advanced voice
applications are typically connected to our customers&#146; existing local and wide
area networks.&nbsp; While we believe the risk of our products disrupting other
traffic or affecting performance of these networks is low, such problems could
occur.&#160; Such an event could cause
significant disruption to our customers&#146; operations, including loss of revenue,
or the inability to access critical services such as 911 emergency
services.&nbsp; In turn, these disruptions could result in reduced customer
satisfaction, delays in payments from customers for products and services
purchased, damage to our reputation, and potential liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We
expect our gross margins to vary over time.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our gross margins are
affected by a variety of factors, including changes in customer and product
mix, increased price competition, changes in vendor incentive programs, and
changes in shipment volume.&nbsp; We expect these factors to cause our gross
margins to be inconsistent in quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year comparisons.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">If our
dealer agreements with the original equipment manufacturers are terminated
prematurely or unexpectedly, our business could be adversely affected.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We sell communications
systems under dealer agreements with various manufacturers such as Avaya,
Nortel, and Mitel.&nbsp; We are a major dealer for many manufacturers and we
consider our relationship with them to be good.&nbsp; Nevertheless, if our
strategic relationship with our manufacturers were to be terminated prematurely
or unexpectedly, our operating results would be adversely impacted.&nbsp;
Furthermore, these agreements require that we meet certain volume commitments
to earn the pricing incentives provided in the dealer agreements.&nbsp; Failure
to meet these requirements could have material adverse consequences on our
gross margins and overall operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We are
dependent upon a few suppliers.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our growth and ability to
meet customer demand depends in part on our capability to obtain timely
deliveries of products from suppliers.&nbsp; Both Avaya and Nortel utilize a
two-tier distribution model whereby a few third-party companies (super
distributors) distribute their products to their dealer communities.&nbsp; In
the case of one such distributor, they distribute both Avaya and Nortel
products.&nbsp; The limited amount of distribution available for each of these
product lines increases our risk of interruptions in the supply of these
products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We may
incur additional goodwill and other asset impairments.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business has been,
and may continue to be, materially adversely affected by macro-economic
conditions.&nbsp; During the fiscal year we have experienced a significant
decline in revenues in our commercial equipment reporting unit and a sustained
decline in our market capitalization.&nbsp; After completing the annual
impairment test, management determined that goodwill associated with our
commercial equipment sales reporting unit was impaired.&#160; As such we recorded an impairment charge of
$14.8 million in fiscal year 2009.&nbsp;&nbsp;We could experience further
deterioration in this area of our business or other areas of our business,
which might result in additional impairment of our remaining goodwill
balances.&nbsp; Additional impairment charges could have a material adverse
effect on our financial condition and results of operations.&nbsp; See Part&nbsp;II
Item 7 of this report &#147;Application of Critical Accounting Policies, Goodwill
and other Long-Lived Assets&#148; for additional information regarding our goodwill
and other asset impairment charges.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11<a name="PB_11_110035_7091"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our
stock price may continue to be volatile</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historically, our stock
is not widely followed by investment analysts and is subject to price and
trading volume volatility.&nbsp; This volatility is sometimes tied to overall
market conditions and may or may not reflect our financial performance.&nbsp;
It is likely that this volatility will continue.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our
business is subject to the risks of tornadoes and other natural catastrophic
events and to interruptions caused by man-made problems such as computer
viruses or terrorism.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our corporate
headquarters and NSC are located in northeastern Oklahoma, a region known as &#147;tornado
alley&#148;.&nbsp; The region is also frequently the victim of significant ice
storms.&nbsp; A significant natural disaster, such as a tornado or prolonged
ice storm could have a material adverse impact on our business, operating
results, and financial condition.&nbsp; In addition, despite our implementation
of network security measures, our servers are vulnerable to computer viruses,
hacking, and similar disruptions from unauthorized tampering of our computer
systems. Any such event could also cause a similar material adverse
impact.&nbsp; In addition, acts of war or terrorism could have a material
adverse impact on our business, operating results and financial
condition.&nbsp; The continued threat of terrorism and associated security and
military response, or any future acts of terrorism may further disrupt the national
economy and create additional uncertainties.&nbsp; To the extent that such
disruptions or uncertainties might result in delays or cancellations of
customer orders, or impact the assembly or shipment of our products, business,
operating results and financial condition could be materially and adversely
affected.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We may
be subject to infringement claims and litigation, which could cause us to incur
significant expenses or prevent us from selling certain products and services.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Third parties, including
customers, may assert claims or initiate legal action against our
manufacturers, suppliers, customers or us, alleging that the products we sell
infringe on another&#146;s proprietary rights.&nbsp; Regardless of merit, such
claims can be time-consuming, expensive, and/or require us to enter into costly
license agreements.&nbsp; In some instances, a successful claim could prevent
us from selling a particular product or service.&nbsp; We have not conducted
patent searches on the third party-products we distribute to independently
determine if they infringe on another party&#146;s proprietary rights.&#160; Nor would it be practical or cost-effective
for us to do so.&nbsp; Rather, we rely on infringement indemnities provided by
the equipment manufacturers.&nbsp; However, because these indemnities are not
absolute and in some instances have limits of coverage, no assurance can be
given that in the event of a claim our indemnification by the equipment
manufacturer will be adequate to hold us harmless, or that we are entitled to indemnification
by the equipment manufacturer.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If any infringement or
other intellectual property claim is brought against us, and succeeds, whether
it is based on a third-party&#146;s equipment that we distribute or on our own
proprietary products, our business, operating results and financial condition
could be materially and adversely affected.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We are
subject to a variety of other general risks and uncertainties inherent in doing
business.</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the
specific factors discussed above, we are subject to risks that are inherent to
doing business.&nbsp; These include growth rates, general economic and
political conditions, customer satisfaction with the quality of our services,
costs of obtaining insurance, unexpected death of key employees, changes in employment
laws and regulations, changes in tax laws and regulations, and other events
that can impact revenues and the cost of doing business.</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h3>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM
2.&#160; PROPERTIES</font></b></h3>

<h3 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h3>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our principal executive offices and the NSC are located in a 37,000
square foot, Company-owned, single story building located on a 13-acre tract of
land in a suburban business park near Tulsa, Oklahoma.&#160; This facility also houses a warehouse and
assembly area.&#160; At October, 31, 2009 the
building was subject to a mortgage held by Bank of Oklahoma, NA.&#160; In November&nbsp;2009, the Company retired
the mortgage and entered into a credit facility with a new banking institution.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have additional leased facilities located near St. Louis,
Missouri.&#160; In addition to our primary
warehouse and shipping operation, this facility houses sales staff, technical
design, professional services and installation support personnel.&#160; We lease office space for branch offices in
Bellevue, Washington; Richardson, Texas; and Southborough, Massachusetts.&#160; These facilities primarily house sales and
technical personnel.&#160; We also lease other
office space throughout the U.S. for sales, consulting, and technical staff.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-.1pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">ITEM 3.&#160; LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-.1pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;10,
2009, the Company was named as an additional defendant in a lawsuit originally filed
on March&nbsp;16, 2009 by Pangaia Partners against two of Pangaia&#146;s former
employees who subsequently went to work for the Company.&nbsp; The lawsuit was
filed in Superior Court of New Jersey Law Division, Bergen County.&nbsp;
Pangaia&#146;s claims against the Company are made in relation to a Nortel account
to which the employee defendants were assigned when they worked for Pangaia and
which they now service as employees of the Company.&nbsp; Pangaia&#146;s claims
against the Company and the individual defendants include unfair competition,
tortuous interference with prospective economic advantage, tortuous
interference with contract, misappropriation of trade secrets, conversion and
unjust enrichment.&nbsp; In its original claim against its former employees,
Pangaia sought but was denied a preliminary injunction to enforce
non-competition agreements.&nbsp; Pangaia now seeks monetary damages against
all defendants, but has not alleged a specific dollar amount.&#160; A preliminary investigation indicates the
claims are without merit and the Company expects to mount a vigorous defense.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12<a name="PB_12_110058_4141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PART&nbsp;II</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 5.&nbsp;&nbsp;MARKET FOR THE

periods indicated, the high and low sales prices of our common stock as
reported on the Nasdaq National Market.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have never paid cash
dividends on our Common Stock.&nbsp; Payment of cash dividends is dependent
upon our earnings, capital requirements, overall financial condition and other
factors deemed relevant by the Board of Directors.&nbsp; Currently, we are
prohibited by our credit facility from paying cash dividends.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2008 the
Board of Directors approved a stock repurchase program in which up to $1,000,000
could be used to repurchase our Common Stock in open market.&nbsp; The timing
and amount of any repurchases is based on various factors, including general
market conditions, the market price of our Common Stock, Company-imposed
black-out periods during which the Company and its insiders are prohibited from
trading in XETA common stock and management&#146;s assessment of our financial
position and liquidity.&nbsp; The program can be modified, suspended, extended
or terminated by the Company at any time without prior notice.&nbsp; The
program does not have an expiration date.&#160;
Since the inception of the
program, we have repurchased a total of 30,796 shares of our common stock for a
total cash investment of $58,157.&#160; There
was no repurchase activity for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;4,
2010, there were approximately 167 shareholders of record.&nbsp; Since many of
the Company&#146;s shareholders hold their shares in &#147;street name,&#148; meaning that
their shares are held in the name of their brokerage firms for the account of
the individual shareholder, we estimate the actual number of shareholders to be
at least over 2,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-.15pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-transform:uppercase;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;text-transform:none;">EQUITY COMPENSATION PLAN INFORMATION</font></b></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM
7.&#160; MANAGEMENT&#146;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font></i></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In&nbsp;fiscal 2009 we
recorded a net loss of $10.3 million.&#160;
This loss included $17.8 million in impairment charges to goodwill and
our ERP system.&#160; Net of these non-cash
charges our after-tax net income would have been $506,000 on revenues of $71.6
million compared to $2.1 million in fiscal 2008 on revenues of $84.3
million.&#160; These declines primarily
reflect two factors: difficult macro-economic conditions which depressed
capital spending, and uncertainty concerning the Nortel product line created by
Nortel&#146;s bankruptcy filing in January&nbsp;2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to the
difficult market conditions experienced throughout fiscal 2009, management
developed and executed a cost reduction plan designed to aggressively reduce
costs while preserving the key resources necessary to fully realize growth
opportunities as the market recovers.&#160;
Underlying the plan was management&#146;s belief that the challenging
economic environment will present growth opportunities in our service business
as customers choose to maintain rather than replace their existing
communication systems.&#160; In addition we
anticipate customers in all segments will give stronger consideration to
outsourcing the support of their communications networks to reduce costs.&nbsp;
To support these trends, management focused cost reduction on elements of our
operations that would not affect our ability to meet the needs of our customers
in these areas.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Increasing our recurring
revenues through both direct and wholesale services offerings is one of our key
strategies.&#160; We continue to invest in
this area of our business and expect improved growth rates in fiscal 2010 based
on three factors:&#160; a modest economic
recovery will likely create a more favorable overall marketplace; disruption in
the market created by Avaya&#146;s acquisition of Nortel should create opportunities
to increase our base of Nortel repair and maintenance revenues; and the growing
trend of end users to outsource additional elements of their communications
services should create growth opportunities to provide managed services to new
customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Macro-economic conditions
negatively impacted our commercial systems business beginning in the first
quarter of fiscal 2009.&#160; Those conditions
worsened significantly in the third fiscal quarter.&#160; Also, uncertainty regarding the ultimate
disposition of the Nortel product line grew as Nortel began divesting its
assets, including assets which are strategic to the Company&#146;s operations.&#160; Finally, the Company&#146;s sustained decline in
market capitalization continued, reflecting market uncertainty regarding the
value of the Company&#146;s operations.&#160; This
combination of factors prompted the Company to conduct an interim test for
impairment as of July&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; The
Company engaged a consultant to assist in the valuation of the commercial
systems sales and services reporting units.&#160;
The Company used a combination of evaluations to estimate the fair value
of its reporting units, including the following:&#160; a) an income approach by which forecasted
future cash flows are discounted to present value; b) a market approach by
which comparable companies values are compared to the applicable reporting unit&#146;s
values; and c) a market approach by which the Company&#146;s own market
capitalization is applied to the applicable reporting unit.&#160; Based on the results of this work, the
Company determined that the carrying value of the commercial systems sales
reporting unit was impaired, and the services reporting unit was not
impaired.&#160; The Company recorded an
impairment charge of $11 million against its commercial systems sales reporting
unit as an initial estimate at the end of the third quarter.&#160; The Company completed its evaluation of the
fair value of this reporting unit including performing the step II analysis
required by ASC 350 during the fourth quarter and increased the total goodwill
impairment charge to $14.8 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Also, in the third
quarter of fiscal 2009, management determined that its Oracle Enterprise
Resource Planning (&#147;ERP&#148;) system and the related investment were over-adequate
for its current and near-term operating needs.&#160;
The ERP system was originally purchased in 2001 during a period of
hyper-growth and the Company expected to be significantly larger within
three-to-five years.&#160; Those growth
expectations did not materialize.&#160;
Furthermore, the economic downturn presented another setback to the
Company&#146;s growth.&#160; As a result,
management determined that it was likely the investment in the ERP system would
not be realized within a reasonable time frame and was therefore impaired.&#160; At the time of the impairment charge, the net
book value of Company&#146;s ERP system was $6.5 million.&#160; The Company used various outside sources and
its current vendor to estimate the cost of a replacement ERP system adequate
for the Company&#146;s current and near-term operating needs. &#160;This research yielded an estimated replacement
cost of $3.5 million.&#160; As a result of
this finding an impairment charge of $3.0 million was recorded in the third
fiscal quarter of the year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The discussion that
follows provides more details regarding the factors and trends that affected
our financial results, liquidity, and capital resources in fiscal 2009 when
compared to the previous year.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14<a name="PB_14_155256_5796"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Results of Operations</font></i></b></h1>

<h1 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FISCAL
YEAR 2009 COMPARED TO FISCAL YEAR 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues for fiscal 2009
were $71.6 million compared to $84.3 million in fiscal 2008, a 15%
decrease.&nbsp; The net loss for fiscal 2009 was $10.3 million compared to net
income of $2.1 million in fiscal 2008.&nbsp; Discussed below are the major
revenue, gross margin, and operating expense items that affected our financial
results during fiscal 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Services Revenues.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp; Revenues earned from our services
business were $41.1 million in fiscal 2009 compared to $43.5 million in fiscal
2008, a 6% decrease.&nbsp; This decline reflects a 1% or $228,000 decrease in
maintenance and repair revenues, a 15% or $1.6 million decrease in
implementation revenues, and a 17% or $538,000 decrease in structured cabling
revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The decreases in our
maintenance and repair services business, which includes revenues earned from
maintenance contracts and time-and-materials (&#147;T&amp;M&#148;) charges, consisted of
relatively flat contract maintenance revenues and a decrease in T&amp;M
revenues of 5%.&#160; We believe the decline
in T&amp;M revenues was primarily influenced by general economic conditions as
customers reduced spending on non-critical services.&#160; Contract revenues in fiscal 2009 were lower
than expected because of several contract losses and a reduction in the size of
one major wholesale services program.&#160;
These reductions offset program wins with other customers.&#160; In each case, the loss of revenues was due to
divestures of assets or strategic changes by end-users that moved the services
to other vendors.&#160; We did not experience
a significant program loss or reduction due to service quality.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our efforts to increase
services revenues center on our wholesale services offerings.&#160; Under these offerings we partner with
manufacturers, network services companies, and systems integrators to provide a
variety of technical services to our partners&#146; end-user customers.&nbsp; We
have invested heavily in sales and technical resources to create relationships
with current and potential wholesale partners.&nbsp; Once those relationships
are established, we jointly market our capabilities with our partners to
end-users who have requested bids for new services or are renewing existing
contracts.&nbsp; The wholesale services segment is a highly competitive market
and end-users because of their size and prominence can demand both favorable
pricing and high service levels.&nbsp; In most cases, our service performance
is measured monthly, quarterly and/or annually by our partner.&nbsp; To date,
our service ratings have been excellent.&nbsp; However, our experience
indicates that end-users expect excellent service ratings, and pricing drives
most purchase decisions.&nbsp; As a result, we have limited influence in
contract negotiations between our wholesale partners and end-users.&nbsp; This
is a key difference between the direct and wholesale services offerings.&nbsp;
As we experienced in fiscal 2009, growth in our wholesale services business
will likely be choppy and include large contract wins that are partially offset
by the occasional loss of a large wholesale services contract.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The decrease in our
implementation revenues in fiscal 2009 reflects the difficult comparison to
fiscal 2008 which provided over $3 million in implementation revenues
associated with the Miami-Dade County Public School&#146;s (&#147;M-DCPS&#148;) orders.&nbsp;
The rate of decline in these revenues was lower than the corresponding rate of
decline in systems sales, traditionally the primary driver of these
revenues.&#160; We attribute this to
increasing demand for more complex communications systems requiring significant
fee-generating design and engineering services provided by our Professional
Services Organization (&#147;PSO&#148;).&#160; In the
near term Implementation revenues will continue to closely align with the sale
of new systems.&#160; From a long term
perspective, however, as customers displace conventional communications
platforms and adopt more complex systems, we anticipate growth in this area of
our business through fee-based utilization of these highly skilled technical
resources.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our structured cabling
revenues decreased 17% in fiscal 2009.&#160;
This decline is a difficult comparison to our structured cabling
revenues in fiscal 2008 due to the significant contribution to these revenues
by the M-DCPS orders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Systems Sales.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp; Sales of systems were $30.1
million in fiscal 2009 compared to $38.9 million in fiscal 2008, a 23% decrease.&nbsp;
Sales of systems to commercial customers were $21.1 million in fiscal 2009, a
30% decrease compared to fiscal 2008.&nbsp; Sales of systems to hospitality
customers were $9.0 million in fiscal 2009, a 5% increase compared to the prior
year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The decrease in sales of
systems to commercial customers is primarily attributable to the completion of
the M-DCPS contract which produced $1.7 million in equipment revenues during
fiscal 2009 compared to $9.4 million during fiscal 2008.&#160; Additionally, macro-economic conditions and
uncertainty around the Nortel bankruptcy dampened capital spending on
technology.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15<a name="PB_15_155256_2897"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increased sales of systems to hospitality customers in fiscal 2009
reflects our continued success in this relatively mature niche market despite
considerable economic challenges in the hospitality segment.&#160; In addition, our success confirms successful
execution on our strategy to expand into the Mitel product offering.&#160; Mitel has provided us with the opportunity to
work with hotel chains and property management companies that have previously
standardized on the Mitel product line.&#160;
Mitel provides us the opportunity to approach existing customers about
opportunities in other hospitality segments requiring a lower price point.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other Revenues</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; Other revenues were $396,000 in
fiscal 2009 compared to $1.9 million in fiscal 2008.&nbsp; Other revenues
consist of commissions earned on the sale of Avaya maintenance contracts and
sales of equipment and/or services made outside of our normal provisioning
processes.&nbsp; The decrease in other revenues is attributable to a decrease
in the sales of Avaya post-warranty maintenance contracts.&nbsp; Under our
dealer agreement with Avaya, we are incentivized to market their maintenance
contracts to the Avaya customer base.&nbsp; We are paid a commission on these
contracts based on the size and length of the contract and the underlying
equipment covered under the agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We expected a decline in
this segment as we benefited throughout 2008 when many customers accelerated
their purchases or renewals of Avaya service contracts in anticipation of
manufacturer-driven changes in the structure of these service programs.&#160; This is an unpredictable revenue stream that
depends on the expiration dates of existing contracts, installation dates of
new systems, the customer type as defined by Avaya, and the number of years
that customers contract for services.&#160;
While no assurance can be given, we expect sales of Avaya service
contracts to return to pre-fiscal 2008 levels.&#160;
Sales of products provisioned outside of our normal processes generally
reflects sales of phone sets to hospitality customers in which we earn a small,
flat, per-phone profit on the transaction.&nbsp; Other revenues also include
restocking fees earned on canceled orders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross Margins</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; Gross margins were 27.2% in
fiscal 2009 compared to 26.4% in fiscal 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The gross margins earned
on services revenues were 31.1% in fiscal 2009 compared to 28.3% in fiscal
2008.&nbsp; Gross margins earned on Services revenues reflect mixed results
between improved margins earned on maintenance and repair services and
structured cabling, which were offset by lower margins on implementations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of improved
cost controls, revised procedures, and reduced headcounts, we earned higher
gross margins on our maintenance and repair and structured cabling services
revenues.&#160; Implementation gross margins
were impacted by the significant decline in revenues related to the M-DCPS contract.&#160; However cost reductions and on-boarding the
new Samsung service program dampened the impact of lower revenues in this
area.&#160; Similar to the Samsung program,
developing additional billable consulting services that are not directly
associated with new system installations is an important aspect of our services
strategy to create more predictability and higher gross margins in this area.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross margins on systems
sales were 26.6% in fiscal 2009 compared to 26.2% in fiscal 2008.&nbsp; These
margins are slightly higher than our expectations and reflect our continued
focus on systems sales margins through controls around contract acceptance and
margin reviews.&nbsp; We also work closely with our manufacturers and
distributors to maximize vendor support through rebate, promotion, and
competitive discount programs.&nbsp; These programs have been relatively
unchanged allowing us to maximize these discounts and rebates.&nbsp; The
Systems sales market is highly competitive and downward pressure on margins is
a constant in this segment of our business.&nbsp; We believe that the
techniques and disciplines we employ around contract acceptance and margin
reviews will enable us to maintain our gross margins on systems sales.&nbsp;
However, we can give no assurance regarding possible changes in our vendor
support programs or other market factors that could either increase or lower
margins.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A final component to our
gross margins is the margins earned on other revenues.&nbsp; These include
costs incurred to market and administer the Avaya post-warranty maintenance
contracts that we sell and our corporate cost of goods sold expenses.&nbsp;
While we earn a commission on the sale of Avaya post-warranty maintenance
contracts which has no direct cost of goods sold, we incur costs in marketing
and administration of these contracts before submitting them to Avaya.&nbsp;
Corporate cost of goods sold represents the cost of our material logistics,
warehousing, advance replacement of service spare parts, and purchasing
functions.&nbsp; Corporate cost of goods sold was 2.0% of revenues in fiscal
2009 compared to 1.8% of revenues in fiscal 2008.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16<a name="PB_16_155256_3020"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating Expenses</font></u>.&nbsp;
Operating expenses, including $17.8 million in impairment charges, were $36.4
million or 50.8% of revenues in fiscal 2009 compared to $18.6 million or 22.0%
of revenues in fiscal 2008.&nbsp; Excluding the impairment charges, operating
expenses were 25.9% of revenues in fiscal 2009.&#160;
Apart from the impairment, the increase in operating expenses reflects
the following factors:</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>A
bad debt provision of $350,000 in specific response to the Nortel bankruptcy
filing</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Increased
legal fees to support litigation and board governance activities</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Increased
amortization of: the ERP system platform prior to the impairment entry made in the
third fiscal quarter; and intangible assets associated with recent acquisitions
of service contracts and customer lists</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The level of operating
expenses as a percentage of revenues is above our targets and we took steps in
the third quarter to bring these costs more in line with our
expectations.&nbsp; These steps included reductions of our sales force and
sales support staffs, a company-wide suspension of the matching contribution on
our 401k Plan, and a mandatory week of unpaid leave for each employee in the
company during the last 4 months of the fiscal year.&#160; Although rapidly declining systems sales make
it difficult to meet our targets for operating expenses as a percent of
revenues, we consider it tactically appropriate, given our strong cash flows,
to support operating expenses above our targets in the near term so we are
positioned for faster than market growth when economic conditions improve.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest Expense
and Other Income.</font></u> &nbsp; Interest expense consists primarily
of interest paid or accrued on our credit facility.&nbsp; Interest expense was
$100,000 in fiscal 2009 compared to $334,000 in fiscal 2008.&#160; This reduction reflects both lower interest
rates and lower average borrowing during the year.&#160; The cash cycle on the M-DCPS project was
extremely long and forced us to borrow heavily on our revolving line of credit
in fiscal 2008 to meet working capital needs.&nbsp; Net other income in fiscal
2009 was approximately $28,000 compared to net other income of approximately
$24,000 in fiscal 2008.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tax Expense</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; We have recorded a combined
Federal and state tax provision of approximately 39.2% in fiscal 2009 and
fiscal 2008.&nbsp; This rate reflects the effective Federal tax rate plus the
estimated composite state income tax rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating Margins</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; Our net loss as a percent of
revenues in fiscal 2009 was a negative 14.4%.&#160;
Excluding the impact of the non-cash impairment charges in fiscal 2009,
our net income as a percentage of revenues was 0.7% compared to net income as a
percent of revenues of 2.4% in fiscal 2008.&nbsp; This decrease reflects
relatively flat operating expenses on decreased revenues in fiscal 2009.&nbsp;
Our current business model targets an operating margin of 4% to 6% to be
reached in the next three to five years.&nbsp; However, we will have to realize
sustained growth in our revenues, continued improvements in total gross
margins, primarily in our service gross margins, and a significantly slower
growth rate in operating expenses to meet this target.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FISCAL
YEAR 2008 COMPARED TO FISCAL YEAR 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues for fiscal 2008
were $84.3 million compared to $70.1 million in fiscal 2007, a 20%
increase.&nbsp; Net income for fiscal 2008 was $2,056,000 compared to
$1,432,000 in fiscal 2007.&nbsp; Discussed below are the major revenue, gross
margin, and operating expense items that affected our financial results during
fiscal 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Services Revenues.</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp; Revenues earned from our services
business were $43.5 million in fiscal 2008 compared to $37.3 million in fiscal
2007, a 17% increase.&nbsp; This growth reflects a 10% or $2.7 million increase
in maintenance and repair services revenues, a 35% or $2.8 million increase in
implementation revenues, and a 24% or $619,000 increase in structured cabling
revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increases in our
maintenance and repair services consisted of growth in our contract maintenance
revenues of 18%, partially offset by lower T&amp;M revenues of 9%.&nbsp; The
growth rate in contract revenues in fiscal 2008 was lower than expected due to
lower growth in commercial contract revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The growth in our
implementation revenues in fiscal 2008 was due to the M-DCPS contract, which
provided over $3 million in implementation revenues.</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></u></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our financial condition
improved during fiscal 2009 as our working capital grew by 23% to $11.5 million
and we generated $10.0 million in cash flows from operations.&nbsp; These cash
flows included a decrease in accounts receivable of $6.1 million, a decrease in
inventory of $343,000 and an increase in unearned revenue of $1.5 million.&#160; These positive cash flows were partially
offset by a decrease in accounts payable of $956,000; a decrease in accrued
liabilities of $399,000; and other changes in working capital items, which
netted a decrease in cash of $390,000.&#160;
The impairment charge to goodwill and other assets of $17.8 million and
the related $6.8 million decrease in deferred tax liabilities did not impact
cash flows in the period.&#160; Other non-cash
charges included amortization of $1.2 million; depreciation of $1.0 million;
provisions for doubtful accounts receivable and obsolete inventories of
$562,000; stock-based compensation of $284,000; and a loss on the sale of
assets of $4,000.&#160; We used these positive
cash flows to reduce borrowings on our working capital line of credit by $2.5
million; to make asset purchases of capitalized hospitality service contracts
as well as certain net assets of Summatis, together totaling $1.55 million;
acquire capital assets of $896,000; reduce our mortgage balance through
scheduled principal payments by $171,000; and fund other financing and
investing activities of $201,000.&#160; The
acquisition of capital assets included $607,000 spent as part of normal
replacement of our information technology infrastructure and headquarters
facility improvements.&#160; The remaining
$288,000 was spent on our ERP implementation.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As noted above, our
deferred tax liabilities decreased $6.8 million during fiscal 2009 and the
balance of our noncurrent deferred tax asset was $739,000 at October&nbsp;31,
2009.&nbsp; Most of this balance and the annual change in this account is due
to the difference in accounting for Goodwill between generally accepted
accounting principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;) and the U.S. tax code.&nbsp; Under GAAP,
Goodwill is not amortized, but instead is evaluated for impairment.&nbsp; This
evaluation is conducted as conditions warrant, but not less than
annually.&nbsp; The deferred tax liability associated with Goodwill accounting
will not be reduced unless the Company records an additional impairment charge
to Goodwill.&#160; In Fiscal year 2009,
goodwill impairment charges of $14.8 million were recorded.&#160; For tax purposes, Goodwill is amortized on a
straight-line basis over 15 years.&nbsp; As a result, the Company receives a
tax deduction of approximately 1/15th of its Goodwill balance each year in its
tax return.&nbsp; Deductions taken on the tax return of approximately $1.8
million annually for amortization is recognized in the balance sheet as a
reduction to the deferred tax asset.&nbsp; The amount recorded in the
noncurrent deferred taxes is the difference between the impairment recorded for
book purposes and the tax amortization multiplied by the effective tax
rate.&nbsp; This difference is recorded as a non current item because under
GAAP deferred taxes are recorded as current or noncurrent based on the
classification of the asset or liability which generated the deferred tax item.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2009
there were no outstanding draws on our working capital revolver.&#160; We believe our cash balances and available
borrowing capacity are sufficient to support our operating requirements for the
foreseeable future.&#160; On November&nbsp;6,
2009 we replaced our previous credit facility with a new loan agreement with a
new banking institution. The new loan agreement consists of an $8.5 million
revolving credit agreement to finance growth in working capital.&#160; In addition to the available capacity under
our working capital line of credit, to finance investments beyond our current
operating needs we believe we may have access to a variety of capital sources
such as private placements of subordinated debt, and public or private sales of
equity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></u></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">See Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 1: Business and Summary of Significant
Accounting Policies for a discussion of the impact of new accounting standards
on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:center;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Application of Critical Accounting Policies</font></u></b></h2>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></h2>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our financial statements
are prepared based on the application of generally accepted accounting
principles in the U.S.&nbsp; These accounting principles require us to exercise
considerable judgment about future events that affect the amounts reported
throughout our financial statements.&nbsp; Actual events could unfold quite differently
than our judgments predicted.&nbsp; Therefore, the estimates and assumptions
inherent in the financial statements included in this report could be
materially different once actual events unfold.&nbsp; We believe the following
policies may involve a higher degree of judgment and complexity in their
application and represent critical accounting policies used in the preparation
of our financial statements.&nbsp; If different assumptions or estimates were
used, our financial statements could be materially different from those
included in this report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue
Recognition</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;
We recognize revenues from equipment sales based on shipment of the equipment,
which is generally easily determined.&nbsp; Revenues from installation and
service activities are recognized based upon completion of the activity, which
sometimes requires judgment on our part.&nbsp; Revenues from maintenance
contracts are recognized ratably over the term of the underlying contract.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Collectability of
Accounts Receivable</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;
We must make judgments about the collectability of our accounts receivable to
be able to present them at their net realizable value on the balance
sheet.&nbsp; To do this, we carefully analyze the aging of our customer
accounts, try to understand why accounts have not been paid, and review historical
bad debt problems.&nbsp; From this analysis, we record an estimated allowance
for receivables that we believe will ultimately become uncollectible.&nbsp; We
actively manage our accounts receivable to minimize our credit risks and
believe that our current allowance for doubtful accounts is fairly stated.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Realizability of
Inventory Values</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;
We make judgments about the ultimate realizability of our inventory in order to
record our inventory at its lower of cost or market.&nbsp; These judgments
involve reviewing current demand for our products in comparison to present
inventory levels and reviewing inventory costs compared to current market
values. We maintain a significant inventory of used and refurbished parts for
which these assessments require a high degree of judgment.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">19<a name="PB_19_155256_7608"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
