<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill and Other
Long-lived Assets</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp;
We have a significant amount of goodwill on our balance sheet resulting from
acquisitions made between fiscal 2000 and 2009.&nbsp; The Company accounts for
goodwill under the provisions of Accounting Standards Codification (&#147;ASC&#148;) 350,
&#147;Intangibles &#151; Goodwill and Other&#148;.&#160; Goodwill recorded as a part of a business
combination is not amortized, but instead is subject to at least an annual
assessment for impairment by applying a fair-value-based test.&#160; The test for goodwill impairment is a
two-step analysis process.&#160; The first
step of the analysis is to determine if a potential impairment exists for a
reporting unit by comparing the fair value of the unit with the carrying value
of the unit.&#160; The goodwill of the
reporting unit is not considered to have a potential impairment if the fair
value of a reporting unit exceeds its carrying amount and the second step of
the impairment test is not necessary.&#160; If
the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds the fair value of the unit, the
second step is performed to determine if goodwill is impaired and to measure
the amount, if any, of impairment loss to recognize.&#160; The second step of the analysis compares the
implied fair value of goodwill with the carrying amount of goodwill.&#160; The implied fair value of goodwill is
determined by allocating all the assets and liabilities, including any
unrecognized intangible assets, to the reporting unit.&#160; If the implied fair value of goodwill exceeds
the carrying amount, then goodwill is not considered impaired.&#160; If the carrying amount of goodwill exceeds
the implied fair value, goodwill is considered impaired and an impairment loss
is recognized in an amount equal to the excess of the carrying amount over the
implied fair value.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Macro-economic conditions
negatively impacted our commercial systems business beginning in the first
quarter of fiscal 2009.&#160; Those conditions
worsened significantly in the third fiscal quarter.&#160; Also, uncertainty regarding the ultimate
disposition of the Nortel product line grew as Nortel began divesting its
assets, including assets which are strategic to the Company&#146;s operations.&#160; Finally, the Company&#146;s sustained decline in
market capitalization continued, reflecting market uncertainty regarding the
value of the Company&#146;s operations.&#160; This
combination of factors prompted the Company to conduct an interim test for
impairment as of July&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; The
Company engaged a consultant to assist in the valuation of the commercial systems
sales and services reporting units.&#160; The
Company used a combination of evaluations to estimate the fair value of its
reporting units, including the following:&#160;
a) an income approach by which forecasted future cash flows are
discounted to present value; b) a market approach by which comparable companies
values are compared to the applicable reporting unit&#146;s values; and c) a market
approach by which the Company&#146;s own market capitalization is applied to the
applicable reporting unit.&#160; Based on the
results of this work, the Company determined that the carrying value of the
commercial systems sales reporting unit was impaired, and the services
reporting unit was not impaired.&#160; The
Company recorded an impairment charge of $11 million against its commercial systems
sales reporting unit as an initial estimate at the end of the third
quarter.&#160; The Company completed its
evaluation of the fair value of this reporting unit including performing the
step II analysis required by ASC 350 during the fourth quarter and increased
the total goodwill impairment charge to $14.8 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have recorded property
and equipment costs at historical cost less accumulated depreciation or
amortization.&nbsp; The determination of useful economic lives and whether or
not these assets are impaired involves significant judgment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with
ASC&nbsp;360, &#147;Impairment or Disposal of Long-Lived Assets&#148;, an impairment loss
on long-lived assets used in operations is recorded when events and
circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the asset may not be
recoverable.&#160; During the third fiscal
quarter, it was determined that certain identifiable assets related to our ERP
platform were impaired because the Company estimates that full cost of the system
cannot be reasonably recovered based on near-term projected financial
results.&nbsp; An impairment charge of $3.0 million was recorded to reduce the
Company&#146;s carrying value of this asset to the mid-point of management&#146;s
estimate of the replacement cost of an ERP system that would be adequate for the
Company&#146;s current and near-term operating needs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accruals for
Contractual Obligations and Contingent Liabilities</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&nbsp; On products assembled or
installed by us, we have varying degrees of warranty obligations.&nbsp; We use
historical trends and make other judgments to estimate our liability for such
obligations.&nbsp; We also must record estimated liabilities for many forms of
Federal, state, and local taxes.&nbsp; Our ultimate liability for these taxes
depends upon a number of factors, including the interpretation of statutes and
the mix of our taxable income between higher and lower taxing
jurisdictions.&nbsp; In the normal course of business, we can be a party to
threatened or actual litigation.&nbsp; In such cases, we evaluate our potential
liability, if any, and determine if an estimate of that liability should be
recorded in our financial statements.&nbsp; Estimating both the probability of
our liability and the potential amount of the liability are highly subjective
exercises and are evaluated frequently as the underlying circumstances change.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">20<a name="PB_20_155256_8146"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM
9.&#160; CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH
ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM
9A(T).&#160; CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We carried out, under the
supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief
Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, an evaluation of our disclosure
controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;under
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;)) as of the
end of our fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2009.&nbsp; Based upon our
evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have
concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective to ensure
that information required to be disclosed in reports that we file or submit
under the Exchange Act are recorded, processed, summarized and reported within
the time periods specified in Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;Commission&#148;)
rules&nbsp;and forms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Controls</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were no significant
changes in our internal controls or in other factors that could significantly
affect these controls subsequent to the date of their evaluation. There were no
significant deficiencies or material weaknesses, and therefore, there were no
corrective actions taken.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Management Report on Internal Control over Financial
Reporting</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management is
responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over
financial reporting. Internal control over financial reporting is defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and
15d-15(f)&nbsp;promulgated under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as
amended, as a process designed by, or under the supervision of, a company&#146;s
principal executive and principal financial officers and effected by a company&#146;s
board, management and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding
the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements
for external purposes in accordance with GAAP and includes those policies and
procedures that:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Pertain to the
maintenance of records that in reasonable detail accurately and fairly reflect
the transactions and dispositions of the assets of a company;</p>

<p align="left" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Provide
reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit
preparation of financial statements in accordance with GAAP, and that receipts
and expenditures of a company are being made only in accordance with
authorizations of management and directors of a company; and</p>

<p align="left" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Provide
reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized
acquisition, use or disposition of a company&#146;s assets that could have a
material effect on the financial statements.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of its inherent
limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or
detect misstatements.&nbsp; Projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to
future periods are subject to the risks that controls may become inadequate
because of changes in conditions or that the degree of compliance with the
policies or procedures may deteriorate.&nbsp; Our management assessed the
effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of October&nbsp;31,
2009.&nbsp; In making this assessment, our management used criteria set forth
by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO)
in Internal Control-Integrated Framework.&nbsp; Based on its assessment, our
management believes that, as of October&nbsp;31, 2009, our internal control
over financial reporting was effective based on those criteria.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This annual report does
not include an attestation report of the Company&#146;s independent registered
public accounting firm regarding internal control over financial
reporting.&nbsp; Management&#146;s report was not subject to attestation by the
Company&#146;s independent registered public accounting firm pursuant to temporary rules&nbsp;of
the Securities and Exchange Commission that permit the Company to provide only
management&#146;s report in this Annual Report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 9B.&#160; OTHER INFORMATION</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 11.&#160;
EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.15pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Information required by this Item
is incorporated by reference to the Proxy Statement under the sections &#147;Executive
Compensation&#148; and &#147;Director Compensation,&#148;
and to the discussion &#147;Compensation Committee Interlocks&#148; under the section &#147;Corporate
Governance&#148;.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.15pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM&nbsp;12.&#160;
SECURITY OWNERSHIP OF CERTAIN BENEFICIAL OWNERS AND MANAGEMENT AND
RELATED STOCKHOLDER MATTERS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.15pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Information relating to Equity
Compensation Plans required by this Item is included in Part&nbsp;II of this
Report in the table entitled &#147;Equity Compensation Plan Information&#148; under the
caption &#147;Market for the Registrant&#146;s Common Stock and Related Stockholder
Matters.&#148;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.15pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="letter-spacing:-.15pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Other information required by this
Item is incorporated by reference to the Proxy Statement under the section &#147;Security
Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">REPORT
OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_111928"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the Board of Directors
and Shareholders of</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">XETA Technologies,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of XETA
Technologies,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiary as of October&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008,
and the related consolidated statements of operations, shareholders&#146; equity and
cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended October&nbsp;31,
2009.&nbsp; These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s
management.&nbsp; Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these
financial statements based on our audits.&nbsp; Tullius Taylor Sartain&nbsp;&amp;
Sartain LLP audited the financial statements of XETA Technologies,&nbsp;Inc.
for the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2007, and merged with Hogan&nbsp;&amp;
Slovacek P.C. to form HoganTaylor LLP effective January&nbsp;7, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public
Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&nbsp; Those standards
require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about
whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement.&#160; The Company is not required to have, nor were
we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial
reporting.&#160; Our audits included
consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis for
designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not
for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#146;s
internal control over financial reporting.&#160;
Accordingly, we express no such opinion.&#160;
An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the
amounts and disclosures in the financial statements.&nbsp; An audit also
includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made
by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement
presentation.&nbsp; We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for
our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to
above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of XETA
Technologies,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiary as of October&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008,
and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three
years in the period ended October&nbsp;31, 2009, in conformity with U.S.
generally accepted accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">XETA TECHNOLOGIES, INC. AND
SUBSIDIARY</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTES TO
CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b><a name="NotesToConsolidatedFinancialState_111813"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">FOR THE THREE YEARS ENDED OCTOBER
31, 2009</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.&#160; <u>BUSINESS AND SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT
ACCOUNTING POLICIES:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Business</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">XETA Technologies,&nbsp;Inc.
(&#147;XETA&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) is a leading integrator of advanced communications technologies
with nationwide sales and service.&#160; XETA
serves a diverse group of business clients in sales, engineering, project
management, implementation, and service support.&#160; The Company sells products produced by a
variety of manufacturers including Avaya,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Avaya&#148;), Nortel Networks
Corporation (&#147;Nortel&#148;), and Mitel Corporation (&#147;Mitel&#148;).&#160; In addition, the Company manufactures and
markets a line of proprietary call accounting systems to the hospitality
industry.&#160; XETA is an Oklahoma
corporation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Xetacom,&nbsp;Inc. is a wholly-owned dormant subsidiary of the Company.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and cash equivalents
consist of money-market accounts and commercial bank accounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair Value of Financial
Instruments</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following methods and assumptions were used to estimate the fair
value of each class of financial instruments for which it is practicable to
estimate the value:</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying value of
cash and cash equivalents, customer deposits, trade accounts receivable,
sales-type leases, accounts payable and short-term debt approximate their
respective fair values due to their short maturities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based upon the borrowing
rates currently available to the Company for bank loans with similar terms and
average maturities, the fair value of the long-term debt approximates the
carrying value.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company earns
revenues from the sale and installation of communications systems, the sale of
maintenance contracts, and the sale of services on a time-and-materials (&#147;T&amp;M&#148;)
basis.&#160; The Company typically sells
communications systems under single contracts to provide the equipment and the
installation services; however, the installation and any associated
professional services and project management services are priced independently
from the equipment based on the market price for those services.&#160; The installation of the systems sold by the
Company can be outsourced to a third party either by the Company under a
subcontractor arrangement or by the customer under arrangements in which
vendors bid separately for the provision of the equipment from the installation
and related services.&#160; Accounting
Standards Codification (&#147;ASC&#148;) 605-25, &#147;Revenue Recognition - Multiple-Element
Arrangements&#148;, addresses certain aspects of accounting by a vendor for arrangements
with multiple revenue-generating elements, such as those including products
with installation.&#160; Revenue is recognized
for each element of the transaction based on its relative fair value.&#160; The revenue associated with each delivered
element should be recognized separately if it has stand-alone value to the
customer, there is evidence of the fair value of the undelivered element, the
delivery or performance of the undelivered element is considered probable and
performance is substantially under the Company&#146;s control and is not essential
to the functionality of the delivered element.&#160;
Under these guidelines, the Company recognizes systems sales revenue
upon shipment of the equipment and installation services revenues upon
completion of the installation of the system.&#160;
Services revenues earned from maintenance contracts are recognized
ratably over the term of the underlying contract on a straight-line basis.&#160; Revenues earned from services provided on a
T&amp;M basis are recognized as those services are provided.&#160; The Company recognizes revenue from
sales-type leases as discussed below under the caption &#147;Lease Accounting.&#148;&#160; Revenues are reported net of applicable sales
and use tax imposed on the related transaction.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-6<a name="PB_6_110638_3020"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Shipping and Handling
Fees</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Freight billed to
customers is included in net sales and service revenues in the consolidated
statements of operations, while freight billed by vendors is included in cost
of sales in the consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for
Manufacturer Incentives</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company receives
various forms of incentive payments, rebates, and negotiated price discounts
from the manufacturers of the products sold.&nbsp; Rebates and negotiated price
discounts directly related to specific customer sales are recorded as a
reduction in the cost of goods sold on those systems sales.&nbsp; Rebates and
other incentives designed to offset marketing expenses and certain growth
initiatives supported by the manufacturer are recorded as contra expense to the
related expenditure.&nbsp; All incentive payments are recorded when earned
under the specific rules&nbsp;of the incentive plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Lease Accounting</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A small portion (less
than 1%) of the Company&#146;s revenues has been generated using sales-type
leases.&nbsp; The Company sells some of its call accounting systems to the
hospitality industry under sales-type leases to be paid over three, four and
five-year periods.&nbsp; Because the present value (computed at the rate
implicit in the lease) of the minimum payments under these sales-type leases
equals or exceeds 90 percent of the fair market value of the systems and/or the
length of the lease exceeds 75 percent of the estimated economic life of the
equipment, the Company recognizes the net effect of these transactions as a sale.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company records
interest income from its sales-type lease receivables.&nbsp; Interest income
from a sales-type lease represents that portion of the aggregate payments to be
received over the life of the lease that exceeds the present value of such payments
using a discount factor equal to the rate implicit in the underlying lease.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounts Receivable</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounts receivable are
recorded at amounts billed to customers less an allowance for doubtful
accounts.&nbsp; Management monitors the payment status of all customer balances
and considers an account to be delinquent once it has aged sixty days past the
due date.&nbsp; The allowance for doubtful accounts is adjusted based on
management&#146;s assessment of collection trends, aging of customer balances, and
any specific disputes.&nbsp; For the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2009, the
Company recorded bad debt expense of $460,000 which included $350,000 provided
for potential uncollectible amounts associated with Nortel&#146;s bankruptcy
filing.&#160; This matter is discussed more
fully in Note 2.&#160; The Company recorded
bad debt expense of $22,924 and $0 in fiscal years 2008 and 2007, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property, Plant&nbsp;&amp;
Equipment</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company capitalizes
the cost of all significant property, plant and equipment additions including
equipment manufactured by the Company and installed at customer locations under
certain system service agreements.&nbsp; Depreciation is computed over the
estimated useful life of the asset or the terms of the lease for leasehold
improvements, whichever is shorter, on a straight-line basis.&nbsp; When assets
are retired or sold, the cost of the assets and the related accumulated
depreciation is removed from the accounts and any resulting gain or loss is
included in other income.&nbsp; Maintenance and repair costs are expensed as
incurred.&nbsp; Interest costs related to an investment in long-lived assets
are capitalized as part of the cost of the asset during the period the asset is
being prepared for use.&nbsp; The Company did not capitalize any interest costs
in fiscal years 2009 and 2008 and capitalized $200,000 in fiscal year 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Software Development
Costs</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">External direct costs of
software development, payroll and payroll-related costs for time spent on the
project by employees directly associated with the development, and interest
costs incurred during the development after the &#147;preliminary project stage&#148; has
been completed are capitalized.&nbsp; The capitalized value of software at October&nbsp;31,
2009 was $3.5 million which reflects an impairment charge of $3.0 million
recorded in fiscal 2009.&#160; In the third
fiscal quarter of fiscal 2009, management determined that its ERP system and
the related investment were over-adequate for its current and near-term
operating needs.&#160; The ERP system was
originally purchased in 2001 during a period of hyper-growth and the Company
expected to be significantly larger within three-to-five years.&#160; Those growth expectations did not
materialize.&#160; Furthermore, the economic
downturn represented another setback in the Company&#146;s growth curve.&#160; As a result, management determined that it
was likely the investment in the ERP system would not be realized within a
reasonable time-frame and was therefore impaired.&#160; At the time of the impairment charge, the net
book value of the Company&#146;s ERP investment was $6.5 million.&#160; The Company used various outside sources and
its current vendor to estimate the replacement cost of an ERP system that </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-7<a name="PB_7_110652_7748"></a></font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">would be adequate for the
Company&#146;s current and near-term operating needs.&#160; This research yielded an estimated
replacement cost of $3.5 million and an impairment charge of $3.0 million was
recorded in the third fiscal quarter of the year.&#160; The Company has segregated the cost of the
developed software into four groups with estimated useful lives of three, five,
seven and ten years.&nbsp; Amortization costs of $931,000, $906,000, and
$619,000 were recognized in fiscal years 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock-Based Compensation
Plans</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company applies the
provisions of ASC 718, &#147;Compensation &#151; Stock Compensation&#148;, which requires
companies to measure all employee stock-based compensation awards using a fair
value method and recognize compensation cost in its financial statements.&nbsp;
The Company recognizes the fair value of stock-based compensation awards as
selling, general and administrative expense in the consolidated statements of
operations on a straight-line basis over the vesting period.&nbsp; We
recognized compensation expense of $284,000, $247,000, and $122,000 for the
twelve months ended October&nbsp;31, 2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income Taxes</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income tax expense is
based on pretax income.&nbsp; Deferred income taxes are computed using the
asset-liability method in accordance with ASC 740, &#147;Income Taxes&#148;, and are
provided on all temporary differences between the financial basis and the tax
basis of the Company&#146;s assets and liabilities.&nbsp; The Company accounts for
any uncertain tax positions, including issues related to the recognition and
measurement of those tax positions, in accordance with the tax position
guidance in ASC 740.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unearned Revenue and
Warranty</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For proprietary systems
sold, the Company typically provides a one-year warranty from the date of
installation of the system. The Company defers a portion of each system sale to
be recognized as service revenue during the warranty period.&nbsp; The amount
deferred is generally equal to the sales price of a maintenance contract for
the type of system under warranty and the length of the warranty period.&nbsp;
The Company also records deposits received on sales orders and prepayments for
maintenance contracts as unearned revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Most of the systems sold
by the Company are manufactured by third parties.&nbsp; In these instances the
Company passes on the manufacturers&#146; warranties to its customers and therefore
does not maintain a warranty reserve for this equipment.&nbsp; The Company
maintains a small reserve for occasional labor costs associated with fulfilling
warranty requests from customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Use of Estimates</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of
financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally
accepted in the U.S. requires management to make estimates and assumptions that
affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of
contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and
the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting
period.&nbsp; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Segment Information</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has three
reportable segments:&nbsp; services, commercial system sales, and hospitality
system sales.&nbsp; Services revenues represent revenues earned from installing
and maintaining systems for customers in both the commercial and hospitality
segments.&nbsp; The Company defines commercial system sales as sales to the
non-hospitality industry.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The reporting segments
follow the same accounting policies used for the Company&#146;s consolidated
financial statements and are described in the summary of significant accounting
policies.&nbsp; Company management evaluates a segment&#146;s performance based upon
gross margins.&nbsp; Assets are not allocated to the segments.&nbsp; Sales to
customers located outside of the U.S. are immaterial.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is a
tabulation of business segment information for 2009, 2008 and 2007:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recently Issued
Accounting Pronouncements</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2009 the
Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued Accounting Standards
Codification (&#147;ASC&#148;) 105, &#147;Generally Accepted Accounting Principles&#148;.&#160; ASC 105 establishes the Codification as the sole source of
authoritative accounting
principles to be applied in the preparation of financial statements in
conformity with GAAP.&#160; The adoption of
this statement did not have a material impact on the Company&#146;s financial
position or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2009, the
FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&#147;ASU&#148;) 2009-13, &#147;Revenue
Recognition - Multiple-Deliverable Revenue Arrangements&#148;.&#160; The guidance in ASU 2009-13 amends the
criteria for separating consideration in multiple-deliverable
arrangements and expands required disclosures related to a company&#146;s
multiple-deliverable revenue arrangements.&#160;
ASU 2009-13 is effective prospectively for fiscal years beginning on or
after June&nbsp;15, 2010.&#160; The Company is
currently assessing the impact that adoption will have on its financial
position or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2009 the
Company adopted ASC 855, &#147;Subsequent Events&#148;, which establishes the general
standards of accounting for and disclosures required for events occurring after
the balance sheet date but before financial statements are issued or are
available to be issued.&#160; Under ASC 855 the effects of all subsequent events that
provide additional evidence about conditions that existed at the date of the
balance sheet, including the estimates inherent in the process of preparing
financial statements, are required to be recognized in the financial
statements.&#160; Subsequent events that
provide evidence about conditions that did not exist at the date of the balance sheet but arose after the
balance sheet date but before financial statements are issued or are available
to be issued should not be recognized in the financial statements but may need
to be disclosed to prevent the financial statements from being misleading.&#160; The adoption did not have a material
impact on the subsequent events that we report, either through recognition or
disclosure, in our consolidated financial statement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2008 the
Company adopted ASC 820, &#147;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#148;, which
defines fair value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value in
accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States,
and expands disclosures about fair value measurements.&nbsp; This statement
does not require any new fair value measurements; rather, it applies under
other accounting pronouncements that require or permit fair value
measurements.&#160; The adoption of ASC 820
did not have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial position
or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2007 the
FASB issued ASC 805, &#147;Business Combinations&#148;.&#160;
Under ASC 805, an entity is required to recognize the assets acquired,
liabilities assumed, contractual contingencies, and contingent consideration at
their fair value on the acquisition date. It further requires that
acquisition-related costs are recognized separately from the acquisition and
expensed as incurred, restructuring costs generally expensed in periods
subsequent to the acquisition date, and changes in accounting for deferred tax
asset valuation allowances and acquired income tax uncertainties after the
measurement period impact income tax expense.&nbsp; The adoption of ASC
805&nbsp;will change the accounting treatment for business combinations on a
prospective basis beginning in the first quarter of fiscal year 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2007 the
FASB issued ASC 810, &#147;Consolidation&#148;.&nbsp; ASC 810 changes the accounting and
reporting for minority interests, which will be recharacterized as non-controlling
interests and classified as a component of equity.&nbsp; ASC 810 is effective
for us on a prospective basis for business combinations with an acquisition
date beginning in the first quarter of fiscal year 2010.&nbsp; As of October&nbsp;31,
2009, the Company did not have any minority interests; therefore the adoption
of this statement is not expected to have an impact on the Company&#146;s
consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-9<a name="PB_9_110845_7608"></a></font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-9',FILE='C:\JMS\105931\10-1473-1\task3864541\1473-1-ba-09.htm',USER='105931',CD='Jan  8 12:33 2010' -->


<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2008 the
FASB issued guidance which was primarily codified into ASC 350 &#147;Intangibles &#151; Goodwill and Other&#148;.&#160; The guidance amends the factors that should
be considered in developing renewal or extension assumptions used to determine
the useful life of intangible assets.&nbsp; The intent of the guidance is to
improve the consistency between the useful life of a recognized intangible
asset under the accounting standards and the period of the expected cash flows
used to measure the fair value of the asset.&nbsp; The Company will adopt in
the first quarter of fiscal 2010 and will apply the guidance prospectively to
intangible assets acquired after adoption.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other accounting
standards that have been issued or proposed that do not require adoption until
a future date are not expected to have a material impact on our consolidated
financial statements upon adoption.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-.1pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0pt;">Goodwill</font></u></b></p>

<p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-.1pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill recorded as a
part of a business combination is not amortized, but instead is subject to at
least an annual assessment for impairment by applying a fair-value-based test.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Macro-economic conditions
negatively impacted our commercial systems business beginning in the first
quarter of fiscal 2009.&#160; Those conditions
worsened significantly in the third fiscal quarter.&#160; Also, uncertainty regarding the ultimate
disposition of the Nortel product line grew as Nortel began divesting its
assets, including assets which are strategic to the Company&#146;s operations.&#160; Finally, the Company&#146;s sustained decline in
market capitalization continued, reflecting market uncertainty regarding the
value of the Company&#146;s operations.&#160; This
combination of factors prompted the Company to conduct an interim test for
impairment as of July&nbsp;31, 2009.&#160; The
Company engaged a consultant to assist in the valuation of the commercial
systems sales and services reporting units.&#160;
The Company used a combination of evaluations to estimate the fair value
of its reporting units, including the following:&#160; a) an income approach by which forecasted
future cash flows are discounted to present value; b) a market approach by
which comparable companies values are compared to the applicable reporting unit&#146;s
values; and c) a market approach by which the Company&#146;s own market
capitalization is applied to the applicable reporting unit.&#160; Based on the results of this work, the
Company determined that the carrying value of the commercial systems sales
reporting unit was impaired, and the services reporting unit was not
impaired.&#160; The Company recorded an
impairment charge of $11 million against its commercial systems sales reporting
unit as an initial estimate at the end of the third quarter.&#160; The Company completed its evaluation of the
fair value of this reporting unit including performing the step II analysis
required by ASC 350 during the fourth quarter and increased the total goodwill
impairment charge to $14.8 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impairment tests were
conducted as of August&nbsp;1 for fiscal years 2008 and 2007 and did not
reflect impairment in either the commercial systems or services reporting
units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The goodwill for tax purposes associated with the acquisition of U.S.
Technologies,&nbsp;Inc. (which occurred November&nbsp;30, 1999) exceeded the
goodwill recorded on the financial statements by $1,462,000.&#160; The Company is reducing the carrying value of
goodwill each accounting period to record the tax benefit realized due to the
excess of tax-deductible goodwill over the reported amount of goodwill,
resulting from a difference in the valuation dates used for common stock given
in the acquisition.&#160; Accrued income taxes
and deferred tax liabilities are being reduced as well.&#160; The Company reduced the carrying value of
goodwill by $55,576 for the impact of the basis difference for both the years
ended October&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
changes in the carrying value of goodwill for fiscal 2009 and 2008 are as
follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;14, 2009
Nortel Networks Corporation filed for bankruptcy protection in the United
States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.&#160; The administrators of the bankruptcy have
adopted a business disposal strategy.&nbsp; Under this strategy, the
administrators have segmented Nortel into three business units: Virtual Service
Switches, CDMA businesses and Enterprise Solutions. We conduct all of our
Nortel business through the Enterprise Solutions unit.&#160; On December&nbsp;18, 2009, Avaya completed
the purchase of Nortel&#146;s enterprise solutions business unit.&#160; Nortel is one of our major suppliers, is an
important customer, and its product line represents a significant portion of
our business.&#160; At the time of filing this
Form&nbsp;10-K, our post-petition relationship with Nortel continues without
interruption.&#160; However, management
recognizes the potential impact of Nortel&#146;s filing on the Company&#146;s financial
performance.&#160; Nortel owes XETA approximately
$700,000 in pre-petition accounts receivable.&#160;
On July&nbsp;17, 2009 the bankruptcy court granted our request for
offset of $116,000 in charges we owed Nortel at the time of the filing.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2009 we have recorded
$350,000 as a reserve against possible Nortel bad debts.&#160; Nortel has until February&nbsp;1, 2010 to
file its reorganization plan; however, this date is subject to further
extension.&#160; Until a plan of
reorganization is filed, our ability to assess the probability of recovering
pre-petition amounts due is limited.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are following
developments in the bankruptcy case and will assert our legal rights and
defenses as appropriate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

being prepared for use.&#160; The Company

and 2007, respectively.&#160; Amortization

expense of the software currently placed in service is approximately $545,000
annually for fiscal years ended October&nbsp;31, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The tax effect of
impairment charges recognized in fiscal year 2009 resulted in a decrease in
noncurrent deferred tax liabilities of approximately $7.0 million.&#160; For tax purposes the Company is amortizing
its goodwill balances over a statutory life of 15 years.&#160; The combination of these tax deductions and
lower levels of taxable income generated from operations in recent years has
created net operating losses that are reflected in the Company&#146;s balance sheet
as deferred tax assets.&#160; Management
believes that future operating income will be sufficient to realize these loss
carry forwards and that no valuation allowance is required.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has net
operating losses of approximately $3.6 million which begin expiring in 2025.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8.&#160; <u>CREDIT AGREEMENTS:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2009
the Company&#146;s credit facility consisted of a term loan agreement with a
commercial bank including a mortgage agreement and a $7.5 million revolving
credit agreement to finance growth in working capital.&#160; The revolving line of credit was collateralized
by trade accounts receivable and inventories.&#160;
At October&nbsp;31, 2009 the Company did not have an outstanding balance
on the revolving line of credit and had approximately $2.524 million
outstanding at October&nbsp;31, 2008.&#160;

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2009
the Company was paying 6.24% on the revolving line of credit borrowings and the
mortgage note.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2009,
the Company entered into a one year loan agreement with a new financial
institution, replacing the previous credit facility which was scheduled to
mature on November&nbsp;30, 2009.&#160; The
new loan agreement consists of an $8.5 million revolving credit agreement
collateralized by trade accounts receivable, inventories, and real estate.&#160; Advance rates are defined in the agreement,
but are generally at the rate of 75% on qualified trade accounts receivable and
50% of qualified inventories and real estate.&#160;
The credit facility contains several financial covenants common in such
agreements including tangible net worth requirements, limitations on the amount
of funded debt to annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and
amortization, limitations on cash dividends, and debt service coverage
requirements.&#160; Interest on the new loan
agreement accrues at the greater of either a) the London Interbank Offered Rate
(&#147;LIBOR&#148;) (0.24% at October&nbsp;31, 2009) plus 3.00% or b) 4.5%.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9.&#160; <u>STOCK-BASED INCENTIVE AWARDS:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In fiscal 2004 the
Company&#146;s stockholders approved the &#147;2004 Omnibus Stock Incentive Plan&#148; (&#147;2004
Plan&#148;) for officers, directors and employees.&nbsp; The 2004 Plan authorizes
the grant of up to 600,000 shares of common stock and includes an evergreen
feature so that such number will automatically increase on November&nbsp;1 of
each year during the term of the 2004 Plan by three percent of the total number
of outstanding shares of common stock outstanding on the previous October&nbsp;31.&nbsp;
Awards available for issuance under the 2004 Plan include nonqualified and
incentive stock options, restricted stock, and other stock-based incentive
awards such as stock appreciation rights or phantom stock.&nbsp; The evergreen
feature does not apply to incentive stock options.&#160; The 2004 Plan is administered by the
Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In fiscal 2000 the
Company&#146;s shareholders approved a stock option plan (&#147;2000 Plan&#148;) for officers,
directors and key employees.&nbsp; The 2000 Plan replaced the previous 1988
Plan, which had expired.&nbsp; Under the 2000 Plan, the Board of Directors, or
a committee thereof, determine the option price, not to be less than fair
market value at the date of grant, number of options granted, and the vesting
period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fourth quarter
of fiscal 2009, the Company made a tender offer to holders of certain
underwater options which had an exercise price greater than $2.95, but not
higher than $4.14, in exchange for a new option with an exercise price of
$2.54, a term of 6 years, and a vesting schedule of 50% after one year of
service and 25% after two and three years of service, respectively.&#160; The exchange ratio, the number of old options
surrendered for each new option, was calculated based on the fair values of the
options surrendered and issued under a value-for-value exchange.&#160; No additional compensation expense was
recognized as a result of the option exchange.&#160;
Under the program 292,100 options were surrendered out of a total
eligible number of 386,800 options in exchange for 198,999 new options with
terms outlined above.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 338,100 options
outstanding and exercisable at October&nbsp;31, 2009 under the 2004 Plan and
the 2000 Plan had no intrinsic value.&#160;
The intrinsic value of a stock option is the amount by which the market
value of the underlying stock exceeds the exercise price of the option.&#160; Exercise prices for options outstanding at October&nbsp;31,
2009, ranged from $1.59 to $18.13.&#160; The
weighted-average fair value of options vested in fiscal 2009 and 2008 was $1.86
and $2.24 per share, respectively.&#160; No
shares vested in fiscal 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has also
granted options outside the 1988 Plan, 2000 Plan, and 2004 Plan to certain
officers and directors typically as an inducement to accept employment or a
seat on the Board.&nbsp; These options generally expire ten years from the date
of grant and are exercisable over the period stated in each option.&nbsp; The
following table summarizes information </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
