<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">concerning options
outstanding under various Officer and Director Plans (&#147;O&amp;D Plans&#148;)

outstanding and exercisable at October&nbsp;31, 2009 under the O&amp;D Plans
had no intrinsic value.&#160; Exercise prices
for options outstanding at October&nbsp;31, 2009, ranged from $5.82 to
$15.53.&#160; All the shares issued under the
O&amp;D Plans were vested prior to fiscal 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted Stock</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Shares of restricted
stock have been granted out of the 2004 Plan to certain key employees and executives
to provide long-term incentive compensation opportunities.&#160; The restricted shares vest in equal portions
over three years.&#160; The fair value of our
restricted shares is determined based on the closing price of our stock on the
date of grant and is recognized straight line over the vesting period.&#160; Restricted shares issued to key employees
were 14,500 and 16,905 in fiscal years 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160; In late fiscal 2008, the Compensation
Committee of the Board of Directors established equity ownership targets for
senior executives and designated a portion of any annual bonuses to be paid in
shares restricted stock if the executive has not met his targets.&#160; Restricted shares issued in fiscal 2009 to
executives in lieu of cash bonuses were 24,416.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of restricted
stock activity under the 2004 Plan is as follows:</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">equipment.&#160; These receivables are secured by the cash
flows under the leases and the equipment installed at the customers&#146; premises.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12.&#160; <u>MAJOR CUSTOMERS, SUPPLIERS AND
CONCENTRATIONS OF CREDIT RISK:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Marriott International,
Host Marriott, and other affiliated companies (&#147;Marriott&#148;) represent a single
customer relationship for our Company and are a major customer. &#160;Revenues earned from Marriott represented 10%,
8%, and 11% of our total revenues in fiscal 2009, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.&#160; Miami-Dade County Public
School systems (&#147;M-DCPS&#148;) is a major customer and revenues earned from M-DCPS
represented 5%, 16%, and 5% of our total revenues in fiscal years 2009, 2008,
and 2007, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company extends
credit to its customers in the normal course of business, including under its
sales-type lease program. As a result, the Company is subject to changes in the
economic and regulatory environments or other conditions, which in turn may
impact the Company&#146;s overall credit risk.&#160;
However, the Company sells to a wide variety of customers and, except
for its hospitality customers, does not focus its sales and marketing efforts
on any particular industry.&#160; Management
considers the Company&#146;s credit risk to be satisfactorily diversified and
believes that the allowance for doubtful accounts is adequate to absorb
estimated losses at October&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of the Company&#146;s
systems sales are derived from sales of equipment designed and marketed by
Avaya, Nortel, or Mitel.&#160; As such, the
Company is subject to the risks associated with these companies&#146; financial
condition, ability to continue to develop and market leading-edge technology
systems, and the soundness of their long-term product strategies.&#160; Both Avaya and Nortel have outsourced their
manufacturing operations to single, separate manufacturers.&#160; Thus, the Company is subject to certain
additional risks such as those that might be caused if the manufacturers incur
financial difficulties or if man-made or natural disasters impact their
manufacturing facilities.&#160; The Company
purchases most of its Avaya and Nortel products from two distributors who have
common ownership.&#160; Avaya has one other
distributor that could quickly supply the Company&#146;s business.&#160; Nortel products can be purchased from several
distributors and the Company makes frequent purchases from those other
distributors.&#160; The Company believes that
both its Avaya and Nortel purchases could be quickly converted to the other
available distributors without a material disruption to its business.&#160; Mitel products are purchased directly from
Mitel to receive certain additional pricing advantages, but the products can be
purchased from a variety of distributors as well.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13.&#160; <u>EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENTS:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has two
incentive compensation plans: one for sales professionals and sales management
and the Employee Bonus Plan (&#147;EBP&#148;) for all other employees.&nbsp; The bonus
plan for sales personnel is based on either gross profit generated or a
percentage of their &#147;contribution&#148;, defined as the gross profit generated less
their direct and allocated sales expenses.&nbsp; The Company paid $366,397,
$474,634 and $422,930 during 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively, under the sales
professionals&#146; bonus plan.&nbsp; The Employee Bonus Plan (&#147;EBP&#148;) provides an
annual incentive compensation opportunity for senior executives and other
employees designated by senior executives and the Board of Directors as key
employees.&nbsp; The purpose of the EBP is to provide an incentive for senior
executives and to reward key employees for leadership and excellent
performance.&nbsp; In fiscal 2009, 2008 and 2007, the Company accrued bonuses
of approximately $151,000, $418,000 and $350,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14.&#160; <u>CONTINGENCIES:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to potential
losses related to Nortel&#146;s pre-petition receivables, the Company may be subject
to preference payment claims asserted by Nortel.&#160;&#160; It is routine in bankruptcy proceedings for
the debtor in possession or bankruptcy trustee to assert a statutory &#147;preference
claim&#148; to seek to recover payments made by the bankrupt entity to creditors
during the 90-day period immediately preceding the filing of the bankruptcy
petition.&nbsp; This period is known as the &#147;preference period.&#148;&nbsp; Although
the debtor is entitled to make a claim based solely upon when the payments were
made, the payments are not recoverable if they were made in the debtor&#146;s
ordinary course of dealings with the creditor.&nbsp; Nortel has filed a
schedule showing approximately $1.6 million in payments made to the Company
during the preference period, but to date has not asserted a preference claim
against the Company.&nbsp; The Company has good defenses to any such potential
claim against it, including that the subject payments were made in the ordinary
course of the Company&#146;s business dealings with Nortel.&nbsp; If a preference
claim is brought, these defenses must be argued as to each individual invoice
for which the Company received payment during the preference period.&nbsp; In
light of the fact that a claim has not been asserted and the Company has not
fully evaluated its potential defenses as against each individual invoice, the
Company is unable at this time to determine the extent, if any, of any material
loss that might occur if a claim to recover&nbsp;preference payments was
asserted.&nbsp; Therefore, no provision for loss has been made beyond the
amount discussed above related to unpaid invoices at </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-16<a name="PB_16_113850_141"></a></font></p>

2009 was $202,898.&#160; Amortization of

under the capital lease and the present value of the net minimum lease payments

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15.&#160; <u>RETIREMENT PLAN:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a 401(k)&nbsp;retirement
plan (&#147;Plan&#148;).&#160; In addition to employee
contributions, the Company made discretionary matching and profit sharing
contributions to the Plan based on percentages set by the Board of
Directors.&#160; The company&#146;s discretionary
matching contributions were suspended as part of a cost reduction plan that was
executed in the third fiscal quarter.&#160;
Contributions made by the Company to the Plan were approximately
$521,000, $712,000 and $621,000 for the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2009,
2008, and 2007, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16.&#160; <u>SUBSEQUENT EVENTS:</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with
preparation of the Consolidated Financial Statements for fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31,
2009, the Company has evaluated subsequent events for potential recognition and
disclosures through January&nbsp;5, 2010, the date of financial statement
issuance.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;6, 2009,
the Company entered into loan agreement with a new banking institution,
replacing the previous credit facility which was scheduled to mature on November&nbsp;30,
2009.&#160; The new credit facility is more
fully described in Note 8 above.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;10,
2009, the Company was named as an additional defendant in a lawsuit originally
filed on March&nbsp;16, 2009 by Pangaia Partners against two of Pangaia&#146;s
former employees who subsequently went to work for the Company.&nbsp; The
lawsuit was filed in Superior Court of New Jersey Law Division, Bergen
County.&nbsp; Pangaia&#146;s claims against the Company are made in relation to a
Nortel account to which the employee defendants were assigned when they worked
for Pangaia and which they now service as employees of the Company.&nbsp;
Pangaia&#146;s claims against the Company and the individual defendants include
unfair competition, tortuous interference with prospective economic advantage,
tortuous interference with contract, misappropriation of trade secrets,
conversion and unjust enrichment.&nbsp; In its original claim against its
former employees, Pangaia sought but was denied a preliminary injunction to
enforce non-competition agreements.&nbsp; Pangaia now seeks monetary damages
against all defendants, but has not alleged a specific dollar amount.&#160; A preliminary investigation indicates the
claims are without merit and the Company expects to mount a vigorous defense.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
